In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful, and in Him I seek help

Part One

The Arabian Peninsula

Chapter 1

The Prophet’s arrival at Qubāʾ and the mosques of Qubāʾ and Medina

1Aḥmad b. Yaḥyā b. Jābir said: A group of people of knowledge of ḥadīth, biography and the conquests of lands told me (I have set down their account, abridged it, and answered some of it with the rest) that when the Messenger of God ﷺ emigrated from Mecca to Medina, he stayed at Qubāʾ with Kulthūm b. al-Hidm b. Imriʾ al-Qays b. al-Ḥārith b. Zayd b. ʿUbayd b. Umayya b. Zayd b. Mālik b. ʿAwf b. ʿAmr b. ʿAwf b. Mālik b. al-Aws. Saʿd b. Khaythama b. al-Ḥārith b. Mālik, of the Banū'l-Salm b. Imriʾ al-Qays b. Mālik b. al-Aws, used to converse with him there, so that some people thought he had stayed with Saʿd. The early emigrants among the Prophet's Companions, and the Anṣār with whom they stayed, had built a mosque at Qubāʾ in which they prayed, prayer then being toward Jerusalem. When the Messenger of God came to Qubāʾ he prayed with them in it. The people of Qubāʾ say it is the mosque of which God said: "A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it" (9:108). But it is also reported that the mosque founded on piety is the mosque of the Messenger of God.

2ʿAffān b. Muslim al-Ṣaffār told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us: Hishām b. ʿUrwa informed me, from ʿUrwa, that he said about this verse : "And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and to divide the believers, and as an outpost for one who had fought God and His Messenger before" (9:107): Saʿd b. Khaythama had built the mosque of Qubāʾ, and its site was where a man named Labba tied his donkey. The people of dissension said: "Shall we prostrate in a place where Labba's donkey was tied? No. Let us build a mosque in which we pray until Abū ʿĀmir comes and prays with us there." Abū ʿĀmir had fled from God and His Messenger to the people of Mecca, then joined Syria and became a Christian. So God revealed: "And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief...", meaning Abū ʿĀmir.

3Rawḥ b. ʿAbd al-Muʾmin the Qurʾān-reciter told us: Bahz b. Asad told me: Ḥammād b. Zayd told us: Ayyūb informed us, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, that the Banū ʿAmr b. ʿAwf built a mosque and the Messenger of God prayed in it with them. Their brothers the Banū Ghanm b. ʿAwf envied them and said: "If we also built a mosque and sent to the Messenger of God to pray in it as he prayed in our companions' mosque! And perhaps Abū ʿĀmir will pass by us when he comes from Syria and pray with us in it." They built a mosque and sent to the Messenger of God asking him to come and pray in it. When the Messenger of God rose to go to them, revelation came to him about them: "And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and to divide the believers and as an outpost for one who had fought God and His Messenger..." (he said: it is Abū ʿĀmir). "Never stand in it. A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves. Is he who founded his building on piety from God and good pleasure..." He said: this is the mosque of Qubāʾ.

4Muḥammad b. Ḥātim b. Maymūn told us: Yazīd b. Hārūn told us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said: When the verse "In it are men who love to purify themselves" came down, the Messenger of God sent to the people of the mosque of Qubāʾ and said: "What is this purification for which you are praised?" They said: "O Messenger of God, we wash away the traces of excrement and urine."

5Muḥammad b. Ḥātim told us: Wakīʿ told us, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿĀmir, who said: Some people of Qubāʾ used to clean themselves with water, and the verse "In it are men who love to purify themselves" was revealed about them.

6ʿAmr b. Muḥammad al-Nāqid and Aḥmad b. Hishām b. Bahrām told me: Wakīʿ b. al-Jarrāḥ told us: Rabīʿa b. ʿUthmān informed us, from ʿImrān b. Abī Anas, from Sahl b. Saʿd, who said: Two men disagreed in the time of the Messenger of God about the mosque founded on piety. One said: "It is the Messenger's mosque." The other said: "It is the mosque of Qubāʾ." They came to the Prophet and asked him. He said: "It is this mosque of mine."

7ʿAmr b. Muḥammad and Muḥammad b. Ḥātim b. Maymūn told us: Wakīʿ told us, from Rabīʿa b. ʿUthmān al-Taymī, from ʿUthmān b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. Abī Rāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The mosque founded on piety is the mosque of the Messenger ﷺ.

8Muḥammad b. Ḥātim told us: Abū Nuʿaym al-Faḍl b. Dukayn told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿĀmir al-Aslamī told us, from ʿImrān b. Abī Anas, from Sahl b. Saʿd, from Ubayy b. Kaʿb, who said: The Prophet was asked about the mosque founded on piety, and he said: "It is this mosque of mine."

9Hudba b. Khālid told me: Abū Hilāl al-Rāsibī told us: Qatāda informed us, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab, about "a mosque founded on piety", that he said: it is the Prophet's great mosque .

10ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Madīnī told us: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna told us, from Abū'l-Zinād, from Khārija b. Zayd b. Thābit, who said: The mosque founded on piety is the mosque of the Messenger ﷺ.

11ʿAffān told us: Wuhayb told us: Dāwūd b. Abī Hind told us, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab, who said: The mosque founded on piety is the great mosque of Medina.

12Muḥammad b. Ḥātim b. Maymūn al-Samīn told us: Wakīʿ told us: Usāma b. Zayd told us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from his father, who said: It is the mosque of the Messenger ﷺ, meaning the one founded on piety.

14[No. 13 is absent in the source.] They said: The mosque of Qubāʾ was later enlarged and added to. When ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar entered it he would pray toward the "perfumed pillar," which was the Messenger's place of prayer.

15They said: The Messenger of God stayed at Qubāʾ on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and rode from there on Friday heading for Medina. He led the Friday prayer in a mosque that the Banū Sālim b. ʿAwf b. ʿAmr b. ʿAwf b. al-Khazraj had built; that was the first Friday prayer he held. Then the Messenger of God passed the dwellings of the Anṣār one by one, all of them asking him to stay with them, until he reached the site of his mosque in Medina, where his she-camel knelt and he dismounted. Abū Ayyūb Khālid b. Zayd b. Kulayb b. Thaʿlaba b. ʿAbd b. ʿAwf b. Ghanm b. Mālik b. al-Najjār b. Thaʿlaba b. ʿAmr b. al-Khazraj came and took his saddle, and he stayed with Abū Ayyūb. Some of the Khazraj wanted him to stay with them, and he said: "A man goes with his saddle." His stay at Abū Ayyūb's house lasted seven months. The full (four-rakʿa) prayer was revealed a month after his arrival. The Anṣār gave the Messenger of God every surplus part of their plots and said: "O Prophet of God, if you wish, take our dwellings." He spoke well to them.

16They said: Abū Umāma Asʿad b. Zurāra b. ʿUdas b. ʿUbayd b. Thaʿlaba b. Ghanm b. Mālik b. al-Najjār, chief of the chiefs, used to gather the Muslims near him in a mosque of his, and the Messenger of God prayed in it. Then he asked Asʿad to sell him land adjoining that mosque which was in his charge, belonging to two orphans in his care called Sahl and Suhayl, sons of Rāfiʿ b. Abī ʿAmr b. ʿĀʾidh b. Thaʿlaba b. Ghanm. Asʿad offered that he take it and he would bear the price for the two orphans, but the Messenger of God refused and bought it from him for ten dinars, which he paid from the wealth of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁. Then the Messenger of God ordered bricks to be made, and the mosque was built with them, its foundation raised with stones, roofed with palm fronds, its pillars palm trunks. When Abū Bakr was made caliph he changed nothing in it. ʿUmar succeeded and enlarged it, and spoke to al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib about selling his house to add it; al-ʿAbbās gave it to God and the Muslims, and ʿUmar added it to the mosque. Then ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān rebuilt it in his caliphate with stone and gypsum (qaṣṣa), made its pillars of stone and its roof of teak, enlarged it, and brought gravel to it from al-ʿAqīq. The first to make a maqṣūra in it was Marwān b. al-Ḥakam b. Umayya, who built it of carved stones. Then nothing was changed in it until al-Walīd b. ʿAbd al-Malik b. Marwān succeeded his father and wrote to ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, then his governor of Medina, ordering him to demolish the mosque and rebuild it , and sent him money, mosaic, marble, and eighty craftsmen of the Greeks and Copts from Syria and Egypt. He built it and enlarged it, and put Ṣāliḥ b. Kaysān, client of Saʿdā, a freedwoman of the family of Muʿayqīb b. Abī Fāṭima al-Dawsī, in charge of its work and expenditure; this was in the year 87, and some say 88. Then none of the caliphs changed anything in it until al-Mahdī, commander of the faithful (God's blessings on him), was made caliph.

17Al-Wāqidī said: Al-Mahdī sent ʿAbd al-Malik b. Shabīb al-Ghassānī and a man from the descendants of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz to Medina to rebuild its mosque and enlarge it, Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān b. ʿAlī being governor there then. They spent a year at the work and added a hundred cubits at its rear, so its length became three hundred cubits and its width two hundred.

18ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Madāʾinī said: Al-Mahdī, commander of the faithful, appointed Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān over Mecca, Medina and Yamāma. He enlarged the mosque of Mecca and the mosque of Medina, and the building of the mosque of Medina was completed in the year 162. Al-Mahdī had come to Medina in the year 160 before the pilgrimage and ordered the maqṣūra to be removed and levelled with the mosque. In the year 246 the commander of the faithful Jaʿfar al-Mutawakkil ʿalā'llāh ﵀ ordered the mosque of Medina repaired; much mosaic was carried to it, and it was finished in the year 247.

19ʿUmar b. Ḥammād b. Abī Ḥanīfa told me: Mālik b. Anas told us: Hishām b. ʿUrwa told us, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: The Messenger of God said: "Whatever of Egypt or of any city is conquered by force, [know that] Medina was conquered by the Qurʾān."

20Shaybān b. Abī Shayba al-Ubullī told us: Abū'l-Ashhab told us: al-Ḥasan informed us that the Messenger of God said: "Every prophet has a sanctuary (ḥaram), and I have declared Medina sacred as Abraham ﵇ declared Mecca sacred, between its two lava fields . Its grass is not to be cut, its trees not felled, and no weapon is to be carried in it for fighting. Whoever introduces an innovation or shelters an innovator, upon him is the curse of God, the angels and all people; no obligatory or voluntary act will be accepted from him."

21Rawḥ b. ʿAbd al-Muʾmin al-Baṣrī the Qurʾān-reciter told me: Abū ʿAwāna told us, from ʿUmar b. Abī Salama b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of God said: "O God, Abraham is Your servant and Messenger and I am Your servant and Messenger, and I have declared sacred what is between its two lava tracts as Abraham declared Mecca sacred." Abū Hurayra used to say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I found gazelles at Buṭḥān I would not disturb them."

22Shaybān b. Abī Shayba told us: al-Qāsim b. al-Faḍl al-Ḥuddānī told us, from Muḥammad b. Ziyād, from his grandfather, who was a client of ʿUthmān b. Maẓʿūn and had in his hand a plot of the family of Maẓʿūn in the lava field, who said: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb would sometimes come to me at midday with his garment over his head and sit with me and talk, and I would bring him cucumbers and greens. One day he said to me: "Do not leave, for I have appointed you over what is here, and do not let anyone beat down a tree or fell it," meaning the trees of Medina, "and if you find anyone doing so take his rope and his axe." I said: "Take his garment?" He said: "No."

23[printed "32"] Abū Masʿūd b. al-Qattāt told me: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā al-Madanī told us, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, that the Messenger of God declared sacred the trees between Uḥud and ʿAyr, and permitted the owner of a water-camel to cut ghaḍā wood and what is needed for his plough and his cart.

24Bakr b. al-Haytham told me: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from al-Layth b. Saʿd, from Hishām b. Saʿd, from Zayd b. Aslam, from his father, who said: I heard ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb say to a man he had appointed over the reserved pasture (ḥimā) of al-Rabadha (Bakr forgot his name) : "Draw in your wing from every Muslim, fear the prayer of the wronged for it is answered, admit the owner of the small flock and the small herd, and leave me aside from the cattle of Ibn ʿAffān and Ibn ʿAwf, for if their herds perish they can go back to farming, whereas if this poor man's herd perishes he comes and cries 'O commander of the faithful! O commander of the faithful!' Pasture is lighter on the Muslims than the penalty of money, gold and silver. By God, it is their land; they fought over it in the pre-Islamic period and embraced Islam on it, and they think I wrong them; and were it not for the animals that are carried upon in the cause of God, I would never have reserved any of their land from the people."

25al-Qāsim b. Sallām Abū ʿUbayd told us: Ibn Abī Maryam told us, from al-ʿUmarī, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God reserved al-Naqīʿ for the horses of the Muslims. Abū ʿUbayd said to me: "With nūn." And he said: "In al-Naqīʿ there is a depression of dharaq, which is ḥandaqūq (a kind of clover)."

26Muṣʿab b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Zubayrī told me, from his father, from Ibn al-Darāwardī, from Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, from Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ, that he found a slave cutting in the reserved pasture, beat him and took away his axe. His mistress, or a woman of his household, went to ʿUmar and complained to him of Saʿd. ʿUmar said: "Return the axe and the clothes, Abū Isḥāq, God have mercy on you." He refused and said: "I will not give up spoils the Messenger of God gave me as booty. I heard him say: 'Whomever you find cutting in the reserve, beat him and strip him.'" He made a hoe of the axe and kept working his land with it until he died.

27Abū'l-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī told us, from Ibn Jaʿdaba and Abū Maʿshar, who said: When the Prophet was at Ẓarīb (some interpret it so) on his return from the raid of Dhū Qarad, the Banū Ḥāritha of the Anṣār said to him: "O Messenger of God, here are the pastures of our camels, the grazing of our sheep, and the exit place of our women," meaning the site of al-Ghāba. The Messenger of God said: "Whoever cuts a tree, let him plant a sapling in its place." So al-Ghāba was planted.

28ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Ḥammād al-Narsī told me : Ḥammād b. Salama told us: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq informed us, from Abū Mālik b. Thaʿlaba, from his father, that the Messenger of God ruled in the valley of Mahzūr that water be held in the land up to the ankles, and when it reaches the ankles it is released to the next; the upper does not withhold from the lower.

29Isḥāq b. Abī Isrāʾīl told us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī'l-Zinād told us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Ḥārith, that the Messenger of God ruled in the torrent of Mahzūr that the upper holds back from those below him until it reaches the ankles and then releases it to those below.

30ʿUmar b. Abī Ḥanīfa told me: Mālik b. Anas told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Bakr b. Muḥammad b. ʿAmr b. Ḥazm al-Anṣārī, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ruled in the torrent of Mahzūr and Mudhaynib that water is held until it reaches the ankles and then the upper releases to the lower. Mālik said: and the Messenger of God ruled likewise in the torrent of Buṭḥān.

31al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad al-ʿIjlī told me (p. 10 in source): Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, who said: Abū Mālik b. Thaʿlaba b. Abī Mālik told us, from his father: A dispute was brought to the Messenger of God about Mahzūr, the valley of the Banū Qurayẓa, and he ruled that the water goes to the ankles and the upper does not hold it back from the lower.

32al-Ḥusayn told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth told us, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God ruled in the torrent of Mahzūr that the owners of palms get water up to the heels, and the owners of crops up to the sandal-straps, then they release the water to those below them.

33Ḥafṣ b. ʿUmar al-Dūrī told me: ʿAbbād b. ʿAbbād told us : Hishām b. ʿUrwa told us, from ʿUrwa, who said: The Messenger of God said: "Buṭḥān is on a channel (tirʿa) of the channels of Paradise."

34ʿAlī b. Muḥammad al-Madāʾinī Abū'l-Ḥasan told me, from Ibn Jaʿdaba and others, who said: Medina came near to being flooded in ʿUthmān's caliphate by the torrent of Mahzūr until ʿUthmān built a dam for it.

35Abū'l-Ḥasan said: And a great frightening flood came also in the year 156. ʿAbd al-Ṣamad b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAbbās, who was governor then, sent ʿUbayd Allāh b. Abī Salama al-ʿUmarī to it. He went out and the people went out after the afternoon prayer, the torrent having filled the endowments (ṣadaqāt) of the Messenger of God. An old woman of the people of al-ʿĀliya showed them a place she used to hear people mention. They dug it and found the water flowing underground, and it drained from there to the valley of Buṭḥān. He said: And from Mahzūr to Mudhaynib is a branch that pours into it.

36Muḥammad b. Abān al-Wāsiṭī told me: Abū Hilāl al-Rāsibī told us: al-Ḥasan told us: The Messenger of God prayed for Medina and its people and named it Ṭayba.

37Abū ʿUmar Ḥafṣ b. ʿUmar al-Dūrī told me: ʿAbbād b. ʿAbbād told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers, who said: When the Messenger of God emigrated to Medina the Muslims fell ill there, and those whose illness was severe included Abū Bakr, Bilāl and ʿĀmir b. Fuhayra. Abū Bakr ﵁ used to say in his illness:

Every man is greeted in the morning among his family,while death is nearer than his sandal-strap.

And Bilāl ﵁ used to say:

Would that I knew whether I shall spend a nightin Fakhkh, with idhkhir and jalīl grasses around me,and whether I shall come down some day to the waters of Majanna,and whether Shāma and Ṭafīl will appear to me.

And ʿĀmir b. Fuhayra used to say :

I have found death before tasting it;the coward's doom comes from above him.[Every man strives with his power],like the bull guarding his hide with his horns.

She said: The Prophet was told of that and said: "O God, make Medina agreeable to us as You made Mecca agreeable to us, and bless us in its mudd and its ṣāʿ."

38al-Walīd b. Ṣāliḥ told us: al-Wāqidī told us, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwa, that a man of the Anṣār disputed with al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām over the ashrāj of the lava field. The Messenger of God said: "Irrigate, Zubayr, then send [the water] to your neighbour."

39ʿAlī al-Athram informed me, from Abū ʿUbayda, who said: The ashrāj are the water-courses in the lava fields, and the ḥarra is land strewn with rock. He said: al-Aṣmaʿī said: they are channels from the lava fields to the plain.

40al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad al-ʿIjlī told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told us: Hishām b. ʿUrwa told us, from his father, who said: ʿUmar ﵁ granted lands in al-ʿAqīq until he came to a piece of land and said: "I have not granted the like of it." Khawwāt b. Jubayr said: "Grant it to me." And he granted it to him.

41al-Ḥusayn told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: ʿUmar granted al-ʿAqīq from its upper to its lower end.

42al-Ḥusayn told me: Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, who said: ʿUmar went out to grant lands to the people and al-Zubayr went out with him. ʿUmar kept granting until he passed al-ʿAqīq and said: "Where are those seeking grants? Since this morning I have not passed a plot better than this." Al-Zubayr said: "Grant it to me." And he granted it to him.

43al-Ḥusayn told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Abū Muʿāwiya al-Ḍarīr told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: ʿUmar granted all of al-ʿAqīq until he reached the grant of Khawwāt b. Jubayr al-Anṣārī and said: "Where are those seeking grants? I have not granted today anything better than this."

44Khalaf b. Hishām al-Bazzār told us : Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh told us: Hishām b. ʿUrwa told us, from his father, who said: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb granted Khawwāt b. Jubayr al-Anṣārī some barren land, and we bought it from him.

45al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh, from Hishām, from his father, the same.

46al-Ḥusayn told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Abū Muʿāwiya told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from ʿUrwa, who said: Abū Bakr granted al-Zubayr the land between al-Jurf and Qanāt.

47Abū'l-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī informed me, saying: Qanāt is a valley that comes from al-Ṭāʾif and pours into al-Arḥaḍiyya and Qarqarat al-Kudr, then comes to the dam of Maʿūna, then passes the edge of al-Qudūm and pours at the foot of the graves of the martyrs at Uḥud.

48Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: Isḥāq b. ʿĪsā told us, from Mālik b. Anas, from Rabīʿa, from some of their scholars, that the Messenger of God granted Bilāl b. al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī mines in the district of al-Furuʿ.

49ʿAmr al-Nāqid and Ibn Sahm al-Anṭākī told me: al-Haytham b. Jamīl al-Anṭākī told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Abū Makīn, from Abū ʿIkrima, client of Bilāl b. al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī, who said: The Messenger of God granted Bilāl land containing a mountain and a mine. The Banū Bilāl sold ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz a piece of land from it, and a mine, or he said two mines, appeared in it. They said: "We sold you only farmland and did not sell you the mines." They brought the Prophet's writing for them on a palm-frond. ʿUmar kissed it, wiped his eye with it, and said to his steward: "See what has come out of it and what you spent, and set off the expenses against it and return the surplus to them."

50Abū ʿUbayd told us: Nuʿaym b. Ḥammād told us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Muḥammad, from Rabīʿa b. Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-Ḥārith b. Bilāl b. al-Ḥārith al-Muzanī, from his father Bilāl b. al-Ḥārith, that the Prophet granted him al-ʿAqīq entirely.

51Muṣʿab al-Zubayrī told me: Mālik b. Anas said: The Messenger of God granted Bilāl b. al-Ḥārith mines in the district of al-Furuʿ; there is no disagreement about that among our scholars, and I know of no disagreement among our companions that on mines the zakāt is a quarter of a tenth. Muṣʿab said: it is reported of al-Zuhrī that he used to say zakāt is due on mines; and it is also reported from him that he said the fifth (khums), like the opinion of the Iraqis. And today they take the fifth from the mines of al-Furuʿ, Najrān, Dhū'l-Marwa, Wādī'l-Qurā and others, following the opinion of Sufyān al-Thawrī, Abū Ḥanīfa, Abū Yūsuf and the people of Iraq.

52al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told me: Wakīʿ b. al-Jarrāḥ told us: al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayy told us, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, that the Messenger of God granted ʿAlī ﵁ four lands: al-Faqīrayn, Bīr Qays, and al-Shajara.

53al-Ḥusayn told me, from Yaḥyā b. Ādam, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, the same.

54ʿUmar b. Muḥammad al-Nāqid told me: Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth told us, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, that he said: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb granted ʿAlī Yanbuʿ and he added others to it.

55al-Ḥusayn told me, from Yaḥyā b. Ādam, from Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, the same.

56Someone I trust told me, from Muṣʿab b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Zubayrī, who said: The well of ʿUrwa was named after ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr. The cistern of ʿAmr was named after ʿAmr b. al-Zubayr. The canal of the Daughters of Nāʾila was named after the children of Nāʾila bint al-Furāfiṣa al-Kalbiyya, wife of ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān; ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān ﵁ had dug this canal and led it to land he had reclaimed and cultivated at al-ʿArṣa. The land of Abū Hurayra was named after Abū Hurayra al-Dawsī. Al-Ṣahwa is the endowment of ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās ﵃ in the mountain of Juhayna. The castle of Nafīs is said to be named after Nafīs the merchant b. Muḥammad b. Zayd b. ʿUbayd b. al-Muʿallā b. Lawdhān b. Ḥāritha b. Zayd of the Khazraj, who are allies of the Banū Zurayq b. ʿAbd Ḥāritha of the Khazraj; this castle is in Ḥarrat Wāqim in Medina , and ʿUbayd b. al-Muʿallā was martyred at Uḥud. He said: It is also said that he is Nafīs b. Muḥammad b. Zayd b. ʿUbayd b. Murra, client of al-Muʿallā; for this ʿUbayd and his father were of the captives of ʿAyn al-Tamr, and ʿUbayd b. Murra died in the days of al-Ḥarra, and his kunya was Abū ʿAbd Allāh. He said: The well of ʿĀʾisha was named after ʿĀʾisha b. Numayr b. Wāqif, ʿĀʾisha being a man of the Aws. The well of al-Muṭṭalib on the Iraq road was named after al-Muṭṭalib b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥanṭab b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿUbayd b. ʿUmar b. Makhzūm. The well of Ibn al-Murtafiʿ was named after Muḥammad b. al-Murtafiʿ b. al-Nuḍayr al-ʿAbdarī.

57Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, from al-Wāqidī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar, from Sharīk b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Namir al-Laythī, from ʿAṭāʾ b. Yasār, client of Maymūna bint al-Ḥārith b. Ḥazn b. Bujayr al-Hilāliyya, who said: When the Messenger of God wished to set up the market in Medina he said: "This is your market; no tax (kharāj) is to be levied on you in it."

58al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām al-Kalbī told me, from his father, from his grandfather Muḥammad b. al-Sāʾib, and from Sharqī b. al-Qaṭāmī al-Kalbī, who said: When Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Jerusalem, exiled those he exiled and enslaved those of the Children of Israel he enslaved, some of them reached the Ḥijāz region and settled in Wādī'l-Qurā, Taymāʾ and Yathrib. In Yathrib there were people of Jurhum and a remnant of the ʿAmālīq who had taken up palms and crops. The newcomers stayed with them and mixed with them, and they kept multiplying while Jurhum and the ʿAmālīq dwindled until they drove them out of Yathrib and took it over, its cultivation and pastures becoming theirs. They remained so as long as God willed. Then those in Yemen of the descendants of Saba b. Yashjub b. Yaʿrub b. Qaḥṭān rebelled, transgressed and were ungrateful for their Lord's favour in the plenty and ease of life He gave them. So God created rats that began gnawing a dam they had between two mountains, with pipes they would open when they wished so that water came to them from them in proportion to their need and will, the Dam of al-ʿArim. The rats kept working on that ʿArim until they breached it. God drowned their gardens, took away their trees and replaced them with bitter fruit, tamarisk and a few lote-trees.

When Muzayqiyā saw that (he is ʿAmr b. ʿĀmir b. Ḥāritha b. Thaʿlaba b. Imriʾ al-Qays b. Māzin b. al-Azd b. Ghawth b. Nabt b. Mālik b. Zayd b. Kahlān b. Saba b. Yashjub b. Yaʿrub b. Qaḥṭān) he sold everything he owned of real estate, livestock and the like, and summoned al-Azd until they went with him to the land of ʿAkk and stayed there. ʿAmr said: "Moving on in search of pasture before one knows is incapacity." When ʿAkk saw al-Azd overcoming their best places, it grieved them. They said to al-Azd: "Move away from us." A one-eyed deaf man of al-Azd called Judhʿ rose and attacked a group of them and killed them, and war broke out between al-Azd and ʿAkk. Al-Azd were defeated and then counter-attacked, and Judhʿ said about it:

We are the sons of Māzin, no doubt,Ghassān is Ghassān and ʿAkk is ʿAkk;they will learn which of us is the more resolute.

Al-Azd had settled at a water called Ghassān and were named for it. Then al-Azd travelled until they reached the land of Ḥakam b. Saʿd al-ʿAshīra b. Mālik b. Udad b. Zayd b. Yashjub b. ʿArīb b. Zayd b. Kahlān b. Saba b. Yashjub b. Yaʿrub b. Qaḥṭān and fought them. Al-Azd prevailed over Ḥakam, then decided to leave their land and moved on, a group of them remaining with them. Then they came to Najrān and its people fought them, and they were victorious over them and stayed in Najrān, then left it except some who stayed behind for reasons that moved them, and came to Mecca, whose people were Jurhum. They stayed at Baṭn Marr. Thaʿlaba b. ʿAmr Muzayqiyā asked Jurhum to give them the lowland of Mecca, and they refused, so he fought them until he gained the lowland. Then he and al-Azd found the place unhealthy and saw the hardship of life there, so they dispersed: one group went to ʿUmān, one to al-Sarāt, one to al-Anbār and al-Ḥīra, one to Syria, and one group stayed in Mecca. Judhʿ said: "Every time you, band of al-Azd, go to a region, a group of you splits off? You are about to become tails among the Arabs." So those who stayed in Mecca were called Khuzāʿa ("split off").

Thaʿlaba b. ʿAmr Muzayqiyā, his sons and followers came to Yathrib, whose inhabitants were Jews, and stayed outside the town; then they became rich, numerous and powerful until they drove the Jews out and entered the town, and the Jews settled outside it. Al-Aws and al-Khazraj are the sons of Ḥāritha b. Thaʿlaba b. ʿAmr Muzayqiyā b. ʿĀmir; their mother was Qayla bint al-Arqam b. ʿAmr, said to be a Ghassānid of al-Azd, and some say she was of ʿUdhra. Before Islam al-Aws and al-Khazraj had battles and "days" in which they became practised in war and used to fighting, until their prowess became known, their bravery recognized, their courage mentioned, their affair weighty in the hearts of the Arabs, and they feared their sharpness; so their territory was safe, their protégé mighty, and this was because God wished to honour His Prophet ﷺ and honour them with supporting him.

59They said: When the Messenger of God came to Medina he wrote a document between himself and the Jews of Yathrib and made a covenant with them. The first of them to break and violate it were the Jews of the Banū Qaynuqāʿ, and the Messenger of God expelled them from Medina. The first land the Messenger of God conquered was the land of the Banū'l-Naḍīr.

Chapter 2

The properties of the Banū’l-Naḍīr

Properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr

60He said: The Messenger of God came to the Banū'l-Naḍīr of the Jews, with Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and Usayd b. Ḥuḍayr, and asked their help with the blood-money of two men of the Banū Kilāb b. Rabīʿa who were under treaty with him, whom ʿAmr b. Umayya al-Ḍamrī had killed. They plotted to throw a millstone on him, so he left them and sent to order them to evacuate his country, since there had come from them the treachery and violation that had come. They refused and declared war. The Messenger of God marched on them and besieged them for fifteen nights, then they made peace with him on the terms that they leave his country, keeping what camels could carry except the ḥalqa and the equipment, and that the Messenger of God have their land, their palms, the ḥalqa and the rest of the weapons; the ḥalqa are coats of mail. So the properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr belonged solely to the Messenger of God. He would cultivate under the palms in their land, and from that provide the sustenance of his family and wives for a year, and what was left over he put into horses and weapons. The Messenger of God granted from the land of the Banū'l-Naḍīr to Abū Bakr, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿAwf, Abū Dujāna Simāk b. Kharasha al-Sāʿidī and others. The affair of the Banū'l-Naḍīr was in the year 4 of the Hijra.

61al-Wāqidī said: Mukhayrīq, one of the Banū'l-Naḍīr, was a learned rabbi; he believed in the Messenger of God and made his property over to him, seven orchards. The Messenger of God made them an endowment. They are: al-Mayθab, al-Ṣāfiya, al-Dalāl, Ḥusnā, Burqa, al-Aʿwāf, and the upper room (mashraba) of Umm Ibrāhīm, son of the Messenger of God, who is Māriya the Copt.

62al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ told us: al-Layth b. Saʿd informed us, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhrī, that the affair of the Banū'l-Naḍīr of the Jews was six months after the day of Uḥud. The Messenger of God besieged them until they surrendered on condition of exile and that they have what camels could carry of goods except the ḥalqa. God revealed about them: "Whatever is in the heavens and earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book..." up to "...and that He may disgrace the transgressors" (59:1 ff.).

63al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Abū Zāʾida, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, about the words "And what God restored to His Messenger from them" (59:6): from the Banū'l-Naḍīr; "for which you did not spur horse or camel, but God gives His messengers power over whom He wills": he told them it was solely for the Messenger of God , apart from others. So the Messenger of God divided it among the emigrants, except that Sahl b. Ḥunayf and Abū Dujāna mentioned poverty and he gave them. He said: As for His words "What God restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and the Messenger" (59:7) to the end of the verse, he said: this is another share, among the Muslims, as God described.

64Muḥammad b. Ḥātim al-Samīn told me: al-Ḥajjāj b. Muḥammad told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mūsā b. ʿUqba, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God burned and cut down the palms of the Banū'l-Naḍīr. About that Ḥassān b. Thābit said:

Easy for the chiefs of Banū Luʾayywas the spreading blaze at al-Buwayra.

Ibn Jurayj said: and about that was revealed: "Whatever palm-trees (līna) you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by God's leave, and to disgrace the transgressors" (59:5). Līna is the palm.

65Abū ʿUbayd told us: Ḥajjāj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mūsā, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, the same.

66Abū ʿAmr al-Shaybānī the transmitter and other transmitters said: This verse is by Abū Sufyān b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and it is really:

Hard for the chiefs of Banū Luʾayywas the spreading blaze at al-Buwayra.

It is also transmitted "al-Buwayla." Ḥassān b. Thābit answered him:

May God perpetuate that for you as a blaze,and ignite the flames in its quarters.They were given the Book and wasted it,so they are blind to the Torah, ruined.

67ʿAmr b. Muḥammad al-Nāqid told me: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from Mālik b. Aws b. al-Ḥadathān, who said: ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb said: The properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr were part of what God restored to His Messenger, and the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against them , so they were solely his; he would spend from them on his family the expenses of a year, and what remained he put in horses as equipment for the cause of God.

68Hishām b. ʿAmmār al-Dimashqī told us: Ḥātim b. Ismāʿīl told us: Usāma b. Zayd told us, from Ibn Shihāb, from Mālik b. Aws b. al-Ḥadathān, that he informed him that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb said: The Messenger of God had three ṣafāyā (choice properties): the property of the Banū'l-Naḍīr, Khaybar and Fadak. As for the properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr, they were held in reserve for his emergencies; as for Fadak, it was for the wayfarers; and as for Khaybar, he divided it into three parts: two parts he divided among the Muslims, and he kept one for himself and his family's expenses, and what exceeded their expenses he returned to the poor among the emigrants.

69al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Sufyān told us, from al-Zuhrī, who said: The properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr were part of what God restored to His Messenger, and the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against them. They were solely the Messenger of God's, and he divided them among the emigrants and gave none of the Anṣār anything from them except two who were poor: Simāk b. Kharasha Abū Dujāna and Sahl b. Ḥunayf.

70al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh told us, from al-Kalbī, who said: When the Messenger of God prevailed over the properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr, who were the first to be expelled, God ﵎ said: "It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering" (59:2); the "gathering" (ḥashr) is the exile. They were among what the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against. The Messenger of God said to the Anṣār: "Your brothers the emigrants have no property. If you wish I will divide this and your properties between you and them all, and if you wish you keep your properties and I divide this among them alone." They said: "Divide this among them, and divide for them of our properties what you wish." Then was revealed: "and they prefer others to themselves, even though they are in need" (59:9). Abū Bakr said: "May God reward you well, company of the Anṣār! By God, we and you are only as the Ghanawī said :

May God reward Jaʿfar on our behalf, when our sandalsslipped with us in the two steps, and slipped.They refused to tire of us, though if our mothermet what they meet from us she would tire.So the man of means is well supplied, and every kinsmangoes to chambers that warmed and sheltered."

71al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Qays b. al-Rabīʿ informed us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God granted al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām land from the land of the Banū'l-Naḍīr, with palms.

72al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā told us: Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God granted from the properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr and granted al-Zubayr.

73Muḥammad b. Saʿd, al-Wāqidī's secretary, told me: Anas b. ʿIyāḍ and ʿAbd Allāh b. Numayr told us: Hishām b. ʿUrwa told us, from his father, that the Prophet granted al-Zubayr land from the properties of the Banū'l-Naḍīr with palms in it, and that Abū Bakr granted al-Zubayr al-Jurf. Anas said in his report: barren land. And ʿAbd Allāh b. Numayr said in his report: and ʿUmar granted al-Zubayr all of al-ʿAqīq.

Chapter 3

The properties of the Banū Qurayẓa

Properties of the Banū Qurayẓa

74They said: The Messenger of God besieged the Banū Qurayẓa for some nights of Dhū'l-Qaʿda and some of Dhū'l-Ḥijja in the year 5; their siege lasted fifteen nights. They were among those who had aided against the Messenger of God in the raid of the Trench, which is the raid of the Confederates. Then they surrendered to his judgement, and Saʿd b. Muʿādh al-Awsī judged between them: he ruled to kill those on whom the razor had passed, to enslave the women and children, and to divide their property among the Muslims. The Messenger of God approved that and said: "You have judged by the judgement of God and His Messenger."

75ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth told me : Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, that when the Messenger of God finished with the Confederates he entered to wash himself, and Gabriel came to him and said: "O Muḥammad! You have laid down your arms and we have not laid down ours yet. Advance on the Banū Qurayẓa." ʿĀʾisha said: "O Messenger of God! I saw him from a gap in the door with dust bound about his head."

76ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth told me: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Khaṭmī, from ʿUmāra b. Khuzayma, from Kathīr b. al-Sāʾib, that the Banū Qurayẓa were presented to the Prophet; whoever had reached puberty or had grown pubic hair was killed, and whoever had not reached puberty nor grown pubic hair was left.

77Wahb b. Baqiyya told me: Yazīd b. Hārūn told us, from Hishām, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab had made a covenant with the Messenger of God that he would aid no one against him, and made God his surety. When he was brought to the Messenger of God on the day of Qurayẓa along with his son, the Messenger of God said: "The surety has fulfilled." Then he ordered him beheaded, and his son beheaded.

78Bakr b. al-Haytham told me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us, from Maʿmar, who said: I asked al-Zuhrī whether the Banū Qurayẓa had land, and he said, rightly: The Messenger of God divided it among the Muslims by shares.

79al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God divided the properties of the Banū Qurayẓa and Khaybar among the Muslims.

80Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ, secretary of al-Layth, told us, from al-Layth b. Saʿd, from ʿUqayl, from al-Zuhrī, that the Messenger of God besieged the Banū Qurayẓa until they surrendered to the judgement of Saʿd b. Muʿādh. He ruled that their men be killed, their children enslaved and their property divided. So that day so many men of them were killed.

Chapter 4

Khaybar

81They said: The Messenger of God raided Khaybar in the year 7. Its people held out against him and delayed, and fought the Muslims; the Messenger of God besieged them for nearly a month, then they made peace with him to spare their blood and leave their children, on the terms that they would evacuate and leave to the Muslims the land, the yellow and white (gold and silver) and the cloth, except what was on their bodies, and not conceal anything from him. Then they said to the Messenger of God: "We have knowledge of cultivation and tending palms, so keep us on." The Messenger of God kept them and dealt with them for half of the fruit and grain, and said: "I keep you as long as God keeps you." When ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ became caliph, plague appeared among them and they committed outrages against the Muslims, so ʿUmar expelled them and divided Khaybar among those Muslims who had a share in it.

82al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭufayl told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, who said: I asked Ibn Shihāb about Khaybar and he told me it had reached him that the Messenger of God conquered it by force after fighting, and it was part of what God restored to His Messenger; the Messenger of God took the fifth and divided it among the Muslims, and those of its people who came down did so on the terms of exile, and the Messenger of God called them to a sharecropping arrangement, and they did it.

83ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Ḥammād al-Narsī told me: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from ʿUbayd b. ʿUmar, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Messenger of God came to the people of Khaybar and fought them until he forced them into their fortress and overcame them over the land and the palms, and made peace with them on the terms that he spare their blood and they evacuate, having what their mounts could carry, and the Messenger of God having the yellow and white and the ḥalqa. He stipulated that they not conceal or hide anything, and if they did they would have no protection or covenant. But they hid a skin containing money and jewellery of Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab, which he had carried with him to Khaybar when the Banū'l-Naḍīr were expelled. The Messenger of God said to Saʿya b. ʿAmr: "What became of the skin of Ḥuyayy that he brought from the Banū'l-Naḍīr?" He said: "Wars and expenses used it up." He said: "The time is near and the wealth was great." Ḥuyayy had been killed before that. The Messenger of God handed Saʿya to al-Zubayr, who subjected him to torture. He said: "I saw Ḥuyayy walking about in this ruin." They went to the ruin and searched it and found the skin. The Messenger of God killed the two sons of Abū'l-Ḥuqayq, one of whom was husband of Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy b. Akhṭab, and took their women and children captive, and divided their property for the breach they had committed. He wanted to expel them from it, but they said: "Leave us in this land to tend it and see to it." The Messenger of God and his Companions had no slaves to work it, and could not spare themselves to see to it, so the Messenger of God gave them Khaybar on terms that they have half of every crop, palm and whatever else the Messenger of God might decide.

ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥa would come to them every year, appraise their crops (kharaṣa) and then make them guarantee half. They complained to the Messenger of God of the severity of his appraisal and wanted to bribe him. He said: "O enemies of God! Would you feed me forbidden gain? By God, I have come to you from the one most beloved to me, and you are more hateful to me than a count of your apes and pigs, and my hatred of you and love of him will not make me fail to deal justly with you." They said: "By this the heavens and the earth stand."

He said: The Messenger of God saw greenness (a bruise) in the eye of Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy. He said: "O Ṣafiyya, what is this greenness?" She said: "My head was in the lap of Ibn Abī'l-Ḥuqayq while I slept, and I dreamed that a moon fell into my lap. I told him and he slapped me and said: 'Do you wish for the kingship of Yathrib?'" She said: "And the Messenger of God was the most hateful of people to me; he killed my husband, my father and my brother." He kept apologizing and saying: "Your father incited the Arabs and did and did, until that went from my soul." He said: and the Messenger of God used to give each of his wives eighty wasq of dates every year and twenty wasq of barley from Khaybar. Nāfiʿ said: When it was ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb's time, they committed outrages against the Muslims and deceived them, and threw Ibn ʿUmar down from the top of a house and dislocated his hands, so ʿUmar ﵁ divided it among the Muslims who had witnessed Khaybar, of the people of al-Ḥudaybiya.

84al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Bakr b. Muḥammad b. ʿAmr b. Ḥazm, who said: The Messenger of God besieged the people of Khaybar in their two forts, al-Waṭīḥ and Sulālim. When they were sure of destruction they asked him to send them away and spare their blood, and he did. The Messenger of God had already taken all the properties: al-Shiqq, al-Naṭāt and al-Katība, and all their forts except what was in these two forts.

85al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ḥarb told us, from Shuʿba, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Laylā, about God's words "and rewarded them with a near conquest" (48:18): he said, Khaybar; "and others which you were not able to take" (48:21): Persia and Byzantium.

86ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us: Yazīd b. Hārūn told us: Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd informed us, from Bashīr b. Yasār, that the Prophet divided Khaybar into thirty-six shares, making each share a hundred shares; he set aside half for his emergencies and what befell him, and divided the other half among the Muslims. The Messenger of God's share in what was divided was al-Shiqq and al-Naṭāt and what was taken with them. Among what he endowed were al-Katība and Sulālim. When the properties came into the Messenger of God's hands he had no workers to do the work of the land for him, so he gave it to the Jews to work for half of what came out of it, and it remained so during the Messenger of God's lifetime and Abū Bakr's. When ʿUmar came, and wealth had grown in the hands of the Muslims and they were strong enough to cultivate the land, he expelled the Jews to Syria and divided the properties among the Muslims.

87Bakr b. al-Haytham told me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that when the Messenger of God conquered Khaybar, the share of the fifth from it was al-Katība, and al-Shiqq, al-Naṭāt, Sulālim and al-Waṭīḥ were for the Muslims. He left them in the hands of the Jews for half; what God brought forth from it for the Muslims was divided among them, until ʿUmar came and divided the ownership of the land among them according to their shares.

88Abū ʿUbayd told us: ʿAlī b. Maʿbad told us, from Abū'l-Malīḥ, from Maymūn b. Mihrān, who said: The Messenger of God besieged the people of Khaybar for between twenty and thirty nights.

89al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ḥammād b. Salama informed us, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Bashīr b. Yasār, that the Messenger of God divided Khaybar into thirty-six shares: eighteen shares for the Messenger of God for the rights that fall on him, the affairs of the people and the delegations, and he divided eighteen shares, each share for a hundred men.

90al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ḥarb, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, who said: I heard Bashīr b. Yasār say: The shares of Khaybar were divided into thirty-six shares, each share comprising a hundred shares. Of this, the Muslims had eighteen shares, which they divided among themselves, with the Messenger of God having the like of one of them; and eighteen shares for those who came to the Messenger of God of the people and delegations and what befell him.

91ʿAmr al-Nāqid and al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Wakīʿ b. al-Jarrāḥ told us: al-ʿUmarī told me, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of God sent Ibn Rawāḥa to Khaybar, and he appraised the palms for them and then gave them the choice to take or give back. They said: "This is the truth, and by it the heavens and the earth stand."

92Isḥāq b. Abī Isrāʾīl told us: al-Ḥajjāj b. Muḥammad told us , from Ibn Jurayj, from a man of the people of Medina, that the Prophet made peace with the Banū Abī'l-Ḥuqayq on the condition that they not conceal a treasure. They concealed it, so he made their blood lawful.

93Abū ʿUbayd told us: ʿAlī b. Maʿbad told us, from Abū'l-Malīḥ, from Maymūn b. Mihrān, that the people of Khaybar took safe-conduct for themselves and their children on the terms that everything in the fortress belong to the Messenger of God. He said: There was in the fortress a household who were bitter against the Messenger of God, and he said to them: "I have known your enmity to God and His Messenger, and that has not stopped me from giving you what I gave your companions; and you gave me your word that if you concealed anything your blood would be lawful to me. What became of your vessels?" They said: "We used them up in our war." He ordered his companions, and they came to the place where they were, dug them up, and then he struck their necks.

94ʿAmr al-Nāqid and Muḥammad b. al-Ṣabbāḥ told us: Hushaym told us: Ibn Abī Laylā informed us, from al-Ḥakam b. ʿUtayba, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God handed Khaybar, with its land and palms, to its people on a half-share basis.

95Muḥammad b. al-Ṣabbāḥ told us: Hushaym b. Bashīr told us: Dāwūd b. Abī Hind informed us, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: The Messenger of God handed Khaybar to its people for half, and sent ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥa to appraise the dates (or he said the palms). He appraised for them and made it two halves, and gave them the choice to take whichever they wished. They said: "By this the heavens and the earth stand."

96Some of Abū Yūsuf's companions told us: Abū Yūsuf told us, from Muslim al-Aʿwar, from Anas, that ʿAbd Allāh b. Rawāḥa said to the people of Khaybar: "If you wish I will appraise and give you the choice, and if you wish you appraise and give me the choice." They said: "By this the heavens and the earth stand."

97al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ al-Miṣrī told us, from Layth b. Saʿd, from Yūnus b. Yazīd, from al-Zuhrī, that the Prophet conquered Khaybar by force after fighting, took the fifth of it and divided four-fifths among the Muslims.

98ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Ḥammād al-Narsī told us: I read to Mālik b. Anas, from Ibn Shihāb, who said: The Messenger of God said: "Two religions shall not coexist in the Arabian Peninsula." ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ investigated that until certainty reached him that the Messenger of God had said: "Two religions shall not coexist in the Arabian Peninsula." So he expelled the Jews of Khaybar.

99al-Walīd b. Ṣāliḥ told me, from al-Wāqidī, from his elders, that the Messenger of God assigned from his share at Khaybar allotments: to each of his wives eighty wasq of dates and twenty wasq of barley; he assigned his uncle al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ﵁ two hundred wasq; and he assigned Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn and others; and he assigned the Banū'l-Muṭṭalib b. ʿAbd Manāf known quantities, and wrote them a firm document of that.

100al-Walīd told me, from al-Wāqidī, from Aflaḥ b. Ḥumayd, from his father, who said: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz appointed me over al-Katība, and we used to give the heirs of those granted allotments, who were registered with us.

101Muḥammad b. Ḥātim al-Samīn told us: Jarīr b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told us, from Layth, from Nāfiʿ, who said: The Messenger of God gave Khaybar to its people for half; it stayed in their hands during the Messenger of God's life, Abū Bakr's, and the early part of ʿUmar's caliphate; then ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar came to them on some errand and they attacked him by night, so [ʿUmar] expelled them from it and divided it among the Muslims present, giving the Prophet's wives a share in it and saying: "Whichever of you wishes may take the fruit, and whichever wishes may take the estate (ḍayʿa)," and it was hers and her heirs'.

102al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told me: Abū Bakr b. ʿAyyāsh told us, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Khaybar was divided into 1,580 shares, and the men were 1,580: of those who witnessed al-Ḥudaybiya 1,540, and those who were with Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib in the land of Abyssinia forty men.

103al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Abū Muʿāwiya told us, from Hishām b. ʿUrwa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of God granted al-Zubayr land at Khaybar with palms and trees in it.

Chapter 5

Fadak

104They said: On his return from Khaybar the Messenger of God sent to the people of Fadak Muḥayyiṣa b. Masʿūd al-Anṣārī, inviting them to Islam; their chief was a man called Yūshaʿ b. Nūn the Jew. They made peace with the Messenger of God for half the land with its soil, and he accepted that from them. So half of Fadak was solely the Messenger of God's, since the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against it, and he used to spend what came from it on the wayfarers. Its people stayed there until ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ was made caliph and expelled the Jews of the Ḥijāz. He sent Abū'l-Haytham Mālik b. al-Tayyihān (some say al-Nayhān), Sahl b. Abī Ḥathma and Zayd b. Thābit, of the Anṣār, who valued half its soil at a fair value; he paid it to the Jews and expelled them to Syria.

105Saʿīd b. Sulaymān told us, from al-Layth b. Saʿd, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, that the people of Fadak made peace with the Messenger of God for half their land and palms. When ʿUmar expelled them, he sent someone who assessed their share of palms and land and paid it to them.

106Bakr b. al-Haytham told me: ʿAbd al-Razzāq told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb gave the people of Fadak the value of half their land and palms.

107al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ibn Abī Zāʾida told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Bakr and some of the descendants of Muḥammad b. Maslama, who said: A remnant of the people of Khaybar fortified themselves and asked the Messenger of God to spare their blood and send them away. The people of Fadak heard of that and came down on similar terms, and Fadak was the Messenger of God's alone, since the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against it.

108al-Ḥusayn told us, from Yaḥyā b. Ādam, from Ziyād al-Bakkāʾī, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Bakr, similarly, adding: and among those who went between them was Muḥayyiṣa b. Masʿūd.

109al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ibrāhīm b. Ḥumayd told me, from Usāma b. Zayd, from Ibn Shihāb, from Mālik b. Aws b. al-Ḥadathān, from ʿUmar ﵁, who said: The Messenger of God had three ṣafāyā. The land of the Banū'l-Naḍīr was held in reserve for his emergencies; Khaybar he divided into three parts; and Fadak was for the wayfarers.

110ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ al-ʿIjlī told us: Ṣafwān b. ʿĪsā told us, from Usāma b. Zayd, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr, that the Prophet's wives sent ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān to Abū Bakr asking him for their inheritance from the Messenger of God's share at Khaybar and Fadak. ʿĀʾisha said to them: "Do you not fear God! Did you not hear the Messenger of God say: 'We are not inherited from; what we leave is charity'? This property is for the family of Muḥammad, for their emergencies and their guests, and when I die it passes to the one who holds authority after me." He said: So they desisted.

111Aḥmad b. Ibrāhīm al-Dawraqī told us: Ṣafwān b. ʿĪsā al-Zuhrī told us, from Usāma, from Ibn Shihāb, from ʿUrwa, the same.

112Ibrāhīm b. Muḥammad told me, from ʿArʿara, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī, that the Banū Umayya took Fadak for themselves and changed the Messenger of God's practice regarding it; when ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ﵁ took office he returned it to what it had been.

113ʿAbd Allāh b. Maymūn al-Muktib told us: al-Fuḍayl b. ʿIyāḍ informed us, from Mālik b. Jaʿwana, from his father, who said: Fāṭima said to Abū Bakr: "The Messenger of God gave me Fadak, so give it to me." ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib testified for her. He asked her for another witness, and Umm Ayman testified for her. He said: "You know, O daughter of the Messenger of God, that only the testimony of two men, or one man and two women, is allowed." So she went away.

114Rawḥ al-Karābīsī told me: Zayd b. al-Ḥubāb told us: Khālid b. Ṭahmān informed us, from a man whom Rawḥ thought to be Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, that Fāṭima ﵂ said to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁: "Give me Fadak, for the Messenger of God made it mine." He asked her for proof. She came with Umm Ayman and Rabāḥ, client of the Prophet, and they testified for her to that. He said: "In this matter only the testimony of one man and two women is allowed."

115Ibn ʿĀʾisha al-Taymī told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Muḥammad b. al-Sāʾib al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ Bādhām, from Umm Hāniʾ, that Fāṭima, daughter of the Messenger of God, came to Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ and said to him: "Who will inherit from you when you die?" He said: "My children and my family." She said: "Then how is it that you inherited the Messenger of God to the exclusion of us?" He said: "O daughter of the Messenger of God! By God, I did not inherit from your father gold or silver or this or that." She said: "Our share at Khaybar and our charity Fadak." He said: "O daughter of the Messenger! I heard the Messenger of God say: 'It is a food that God gave me to eat during my life, and when I die it is for the Muslims.'"

116ʿUthmān b. Abī Shayba told us: Jarīr b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told us, from Mughīra, that ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz gathered the Banū Umayya and said: "Fadak belonged to the Prophet; he used to spend from it, eat from it, return to the poor of the Banū Hāshim and marry off their unmarried. Fāṭima asked him to give it to her, and he refused. When he was taken, Abū Bakr acted regarding it as the Messenger of God had acted, then ʿUmar took office and acted regarding it likewise. And I call you to witness that I have returned it to what it was."

117Surayj b. Yūnus told us: Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm informed us, from Ayyūb, from al-Zuhrī, about God's words "for which you did not spur horse or camel" (59:6), who said: These are Arab villages belonging to the Messenger of God: Fadak and so-and-so.

118Abū ʿUbayd told us : Saʿīd b. ʿUfayr told us, from Mālik b. Anas (Abū ʿUbayd said: I do not know whether he mentioned it from al-Zuhrī), who said: ʿUmar expelled the Jews of Khaybar and they left it. As for the Jews of Fadak, they had half the fruit and half the land, since the Messenger of God had made peace with them on that. ʿUmar assessed for them half the fruit and half the land in gold, silver and saddles, and then expelled them.

119ʿAmr al-Nāqid told me: al-Ḥajjāj b. Abī Minīʿ al-Ruṣāfī told me, from his father, from Abū Burqān, that when ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz was made caliph he gave a sermon and said: "Fadak was part of what God restored to His Messenger, and the Muslims had not spurred horse or camel against it. Fāṭima, may God have mercy on her, asked him for it and he said: 'It is not for you to ask me, nor for me to give it to you.' He used to put what came from it to the wayfarers. Then Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān and ʿAlī ﵃ took office and placed it where the Messenger of God had placed it. Then Muʿāwiya took office and granted it to Marwān b. al-Ḥakam, and Marwān gave it to my father and to ʿAbd al-Malik, so it came to me, al-Walīd and Sulaymān. When al-Walīd took office I asked him for my share of it and he gave it to me, and I asked Sulaymān for his share and he gave it to me, so I gathered it all. I had no property more beloved to me than it, and I call you to witness that I have returned it to what it was."

In the year 210, the commander of the faithful al-Maʾmūn ʿAbd Allāh b. Hārūn al-Rashīd ordered it handed to the descendants of Fāṭima, and wrote about it to Qutham b. Jaʿfar, his governor of Medina: "To proceed: The commander of the faithful, by virtue of his place in God's religion, in the caliphate of His Messenger ﷺ and his kinship with him, is the most entitled to follow his practice, execute his command, and surrender to whomever he granted a grant and gave a charity, his grant and charity; and in God lies the commander of the faithful's success and protection, and his desire is toward Him in acting in what brings him near. The Messenger of God ﷺ gave Fāṭima, daughter of the Messenger of God, Fadak and gave it to her as charity, and that was a manifest, known matter with no disagreement among the family of the Messenger of God; and she continued to claim what was most rightly hers of what was given. The commander of the faithful therefore saw fit to return it to her heirs and hand it over to them, seeking nearness to God by establishing His right and justice, and to the Messenger of God by executing his command and charity. He ordered that this be recorded in his registers and written to his governors. For if it was proclaimed at every season, after God took His Prophet, that whoever had a charity, gift or promise should recall it, and his word was accepted and his promise carried out, then Fāṭima ﵂ is most entitled to have her word believed regarding what the Messenger of God gave her. The commander of the faithful has written to al-Mubārak al-Ṭabarī, the commander of the faithful's client, ordering him to return Fadak to the heirs of Fāṭima, daughter of the Messenger of God, with its boundaries and all rights attributed to it, and what is in it of slaves, produce and otherwise, and to hand it over to Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā b. al-Ḥusayn b. Zayd b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib and Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, since the commander of the faithful has charged them with attending to it for its people. So make known to those near you the commander of the faithful's view and what God inspired him of obedience to Him and success in drawing near to Him and His Messenger, inform those around you, deal with Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā and Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh as you dealt with al-Mubārak al-Ṭabarī, and help them in what brings its cultivation, its good, and abundance of its produce, God willing. Peace. Written on Wednesday, two nights remaining of Dhū'l-Qaʿda, the year 210."

When al-Mutawakkil ʿalā'llāh ﵀ took office he ordered it returned to what it had been before al-Maʾmūn ﵀.

Chapter 6

Wādī’l-Qurā and Taymāʾ

The affair of Wādī'l-Qurā and Taymāʾ

120They said: On his return from Khaybar the Messenger of God came to Wādī'l-Qurā and called its people to Islam; they refused and fought, so the Messenger of God conquered it by force, and God made its people's property booty for him, and the Muslims got furniture and goods from them. The Messenger of God took the fifth of that, left the palms and land in the hands of the Jews, and dealt with them on the lines on which he dealt with the people of Khaybar. It is said that ʿUmar expelled its Jews and divided it among those who fought for it, and it is said that he did not expel them because it lies outside the Ḥijāz. It is today attached to the district of Medina and its dependencies.

121A number of people of knowledge informed me that Rifāʿa b. Zayd al-Judhāmī had given the Messenger of God a slave called Midʿam. In the raid of Wādī'l-Qurā, a stray arrow struck him as he was unloading the Messenger of God's saddle. It was said: "O Messenger of God! Congratulations to your slave, an arrow hit him and he was martyred." He said: "No! The cloak he took from the spoils on the day of Khaybar is burning on him as fire."

122Shaybān b. Farrūkh told us: Abū'l-Ashhab told us, from al-Ḥasan, that it was said to the Messenger of God: "So-and-so, your boy, was martyred." He said: "He is being dragged to the Fire in a cloak he stole."

123ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth told me: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from al-Jurayrī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Sufyān, and Ḥabīb b. al-Shahīd told us, from al-Ḥasan, that it was said to the Messenger of God: "Congratulations to you, so-and-so, your boy, was martyred." He said: "Rather he is being dragged to the Fire in a cloak he stole."

124They said: When the people of Taymāʾ heard what the Messenger of God had done to the people of Wādī'l-Qurā, they made peace with him on payment of the jizya, and stayed in their country, their lands in their hands. The Messenger of God appointed ʿAmr b. Saʿīd b. al-ʿĀṣ b. Umayya over Wādī'l-Qurā, and after the conquest appointed Yazīd b. Abī Sufyān, whose conversion was on the day of the conquest of Taymāʾ [sic].

125ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Ḥammād al-Narsī told me: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl b. Ḥakīm, from ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb expelled the people of Fadak, Taymāʾ and Khaybar. He said: And the Messenger of God's fight against the people of Wādī'l-Qurā was in Jumādā II of the year 7.

126al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām al-Kalbī told me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God granted Ḥamza b. al-Nuʿmān b. Hawdha al-ʿUdhrī a whip-throw's distance of Wādī'l-Qurā; he was chief of the Banū ʿUdhra and was the first of the people of the Ḥijāz to come to the Prophet with the charity of the Banū ʿUdhra.

127ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh, client of Quraysh, told me, from al-ʿAbbās b. ʿĀmir, from his uncle, who said: ʿAbd al-Malik b. Marwān came to Yazīd b. Muʿāwiya and said: "O commander of the faithful! Muʿāwiya bought from one of the Jews some land in Wādī'l-Qurā and developed other land to go with it; you pay no attention to this property, so it has gone to waste and its yield has declined. Grant it to me, for it is of no consequence." Yazīd said: "We are not stingy with the large nor deceived about the small." He said: "O commander of the faithful! Its yield is such-and-such." He said: "It is yours." When he left, Yazīd said: "This is the one who is said to rule after us. If that is true, we have conciliated him; if false, we have rewarded him."

Chapter 7

Mecca

128They said: When the Messenger of God concluded the agreement with Quraysh in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya and wrote the document on the truce, [stipulating] that whoever wished to enter the covenant of Muḥammad could, and whoever wished to enter the covenant of Quraysh could, and that if any of the Messenger of God's companions came to Quraysh they would not return him, while if any of them or their allies came to him he would return him, those of Kināna stood and said: "We enter the covenant of Quraysh and its term," and Khuzāʿa stood and said: "We enter the covenant of Muḥammad and his pact." There had been an old alliance between ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Khuzāʿa, hence ʿAmr b. Sālim b. Ḥuṣayra al-Khuzāʿī said :

O God, I adjure Muḥammadby the alliance of our father and his father, the oldest.

Then a man of Khuzāʿa heard a man of Kināna reciting satire against the Messenger of God, and he leapt on him and struck him on the head. This stirred up evil and fighting between them; Quraysh helped the Banū Kināna, and some of their men went out with them and attacked Khuzāʿa by night. That was one of the ways in which they broke the treaty and agreement. ʿAmr b. Sālim b. Ḥuṣayra al-Khuzāʿī came to the Messenger of God seeking his aid, which led him to raid Mecca.

129Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: ʿUthmān b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū'l-Aswad, from ʿUrwa, in a long ḥadīth, who said: Quraysh made a truce with the Messenger of God that they be safe from one another regarding aghlāl and asilāl (or he said arsāl): whoever came to Mecca as pilgrim, ʿumra-performer or passing through to Yemen and al-Ṭāʾif would be safe, and whoever of the polytheists came to Medina heading for Syria and the East would be safe. He said: The Messenger of God included the Banū Kaʿb in his covenant, and Quraysh included in theirs their allies of the Banū Kināna.

130ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us: Ayyūb informed us, from ʿIkrima, that the Banū Bakr of Kināna were in the peace of Quraysh and Khuzāʿa were in the peace of the Messenger of God. The Banū Bakr and Khuzāʿa fought at ʿArafa , and Quraysh supplied the Banū Bakr with weapons, gave them water and shaded them. Some of them said to others: "You have broken the covenant." They said: "By God we have not broken it. We did not fight; we only supplied them, gave them water and shaded them." They said to Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb: "Go and renew the alliance and make peace among the people." Abū Sufyān came to Medina and met Abū Bakr and said: "O Abū Bakr! Renew the alliance and make peace among the people." Abū Bakr said: "Meet ʿUmar." He met ʿUmar and said: "Renew the alliance and make peace among the people." ʿUmar said: "May God cut off of it what was joined and wear out what was new." Abū Sufyān said: "By God, I have never seen in the presence of a clan one worse than you." He went to Fāṭima, who said: "Meet ʿAlī." He met him and told him the same, and ʿAlī said: "You are the elder of Quraysh and its chief, so renew the alliance and make peace among the people." Abū Sufyān struck his right hand on his left and said: "I have renewed the alliance and made peace among the people." Then he went to Mecca. The Messenger of God had said: "Abū Sufyān is coming and will return satisfied without his need fulfilled." When he returned to the people of Mecca he told them the news and they said: "By God, we have never seen anyone sillier than you. You brought us neither war that we might be on guard, nor peace that we might feel safe."

Khuzāʿa came to the Messenger of God and complained of what had befallen them, and the Messenger of God said: "I have been commanded toward one of the two towns, Mecca or al-Ṭāʾif." He ordered the march and went out with his Companions, saying: "O God, strike their ears so they do not hear, until we take them by surprise." He pressed on until he camped at Marr al-Ẓahrān. Quraysh had said to Abū Sufyān: "Go back." When he reached Marr al-Ẓahrān and saw the fires and tents he said: "What is the matter with the people, as if they were the people of the evening of ʿArafa?" The Messenger of God's cavalry overtook him and took him prisoner. He was brought to the Prophet, and ʿUmar came and wanted to kill him but al-ʿAbbās prevented him; he converted and entered the presence of the Messenger of God.

At dawn prayer the people stirred to make ablution. Abū Sufyān said to al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: "What is the matter with them? Do they want to kill me?" He said: "No, they have only risen for prayer." When they entered prayer he saw that when the Messenger of God bowed they bowed, and when he prostrated they prostrated. He said: "By God, I have never seen the like of today's obedience of a people who came from here and there, not even the Persian nobles nor the horned Byzantines." Al-ʿAbbās said: "O Messenger of God, send me to the people of Mecca to call them to Islam." When he had sent him he sent after him and said: "Bring back my uncle, lest the polytheists kill him." But he refused to return until he reached Mecca. He said: "O people! Submit and you will be safe. You have been come upon, you have been come upon, and you are drawn into a great ... [obscure idiom]. Here is Khālid at the bottom of Mecca and here is al-Zubayr at the top of Mecca, and here is the Messenger of God with the emigrants, the Anṣār and Khuzāʿa." Quraysh said: "And what is Khuzāʿa, the cut-nosed!"

131ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Muḥammad b. ʿAmr, from Abū Salama b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Hurayra, that the spokesman of Khuzāʿa said to the Prophet:

O God, I adjure Muḥammadby the alliance of our father and his father, the oldest.So help, God guide you, with a strong help,and call God's servants to come as reinforcement.

132Ḥammād said: ʿAlī b. Zayd told me, from ʿIkrima, that Khuzāʿa called out to the Prophet while he was washing and he said: "At your service."

133al-Wāqidī and others said: Some men of Quraysh took up arms on the day of the conquest and said: "Muḥammad shall not enter it except by force." Khālid b. al-Walīd fought them; he was the first whom the Messenger of God commanded to enter. He killed twenty-four men of Quraysh and four of Hudhayl; it is also said he killed that day twenty-three men of Quraysh , and the rest fled and sought refuge on mountaintops and climbed them. Of the Messenger of God's Companions, Kurz b. Jābir al-Fihrī and Khālid al-Ashʿar al-Kaʿbī were martyred that day. Hishām b. al-Kalbī said: He is Ḥubaysh al-Ashʿar b. Khālid al-Kaʿbī of Khuzāʿa.

134Shaybān b. Abī Shayba al-Ubullī told us: Sulaymān b. al-Mughīra told us: Thābit al-Bunānī told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Rabāḥ, who said: Delegations came to Muʿāwiya, in the month of Ramadan, and some of us would make food for others, and Abū Hurayra often invited us to his lodging. He said: So I made food for them and invited them, and Abū Hurayra said: "Shall I not pleasantly occupy you with a ḥadīth from your own history, company of the Anṣār?" Then he mentioned the conquest of Mecca and said: The Messenger of God advanced until he reached Mecca; he sent al-Zubayr over one flank and Khālid b. al-Walīd over the other, and sent Abū ʿUbayda b. al-Jarrāḥ over the unarmoured infantry. They took the bottom of the valley, with the Messenger of God in his squadron. He saw me and said: "O Abū Hurayra!" I said: "At your service, O Messenger of God." He said: "Call the Anṣār, and let none come but an Anṣārī." He said: I called them and they gathered around him. Quraysh had gathered their rabble and followers and said: "We will send these forward; if they gain a victory we will be with them, and if they are struck we will give what is asked." The Messenger of God said: "Do you see the rabble of Quraysh?" They said: "Yes." He gestured with one hand over the other, signifying: kill them. Then he said: "Meet me at al-Ṣafā." He said: We went, and no one wished to kill anyone but killed him. Abū Sufyān came and said: "O Messenger of God! The green of Quraysh is destroyed; no Quraysh after today." The Messenger of God said: "Whoever enters the house of Abū Sufyān is safe , whoever shuts his door is safe, and whoever throws down his weapon is safe." Some of the Anṣār said to others: "As for the man, desire for his kin and compassion for his clan has overtaken him." Revelation came to the Messenger of God (when it came to him it was not hidden from us), and he said: "O company of the Anṣār, you said such and such." They said: "That was so, O Messenger of God." He said: "Never! I am the servant of God and His Messenger; I emigrated to God and to you; the living is your living and the dying is your dying." They began weeping and saying: "By God, we said what we said only out of miserliness [clinging] to the Messenger of God."

He said: The people came to the house of Abū Sufyān, shut its doors and laid down their weapons. The Messenger of God came to the Black Stone and touched it, then circumambulated the House, and came upon an idol beside the Kaʿba, with a bow in his hand held by its tip; he began to poke at the idol's eye and say: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever vanishing" (17:81). He said: When he finished his circumambulation he came to al-Ṣafā and climbed it until he could see the House, then raised his hand praising God and supplicating.

135Muḥammad b. al-Ṣabbāḥ told us: Hushaym informed us, from Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUtba, who said: The Messenger of God said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: "No wounded man is to be finished off, no fleeing man pursued, no prisoner killed, and whoever shuts his door is safe."

136al-Wāqidī said: The raid of the conquest was in Ramadan of the year 8. The Messenger of God stayed in Mecca until the Fiṭr, then set out for the raid of Ḥunayn. He appointed ʿAttāb b. Asīd b. Abī'l-ʿĪṣ b. Umayya over Mecca, and the Messenger of God ordered the idols destroyed and the images in the Kaʿba erased, and said: "Kill Ibn Khaṭal even if he is clinging to the curtains of the Kaʿba" . Abū Barza al-Aslamī killed him. Abū'l-Yaqẓān said: Ibn Khaṭal's name was Qays, and Abū Shurayḥ al-Anṣārī killed him. Ibn Khaṭal had two singing-girls who sang satires on the Messenger of God; one was killed and the other survived until a rib of hers was broken in ʿUthmān's days and she died. Numayla b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Kinānī killed Miqyas b. Ṣubāba al-Kinānī, whom the Messenger of God had ordered killed by whoever found him. That was because his brother Hāshim b. Ṣubāba b. Ḥazn converted and witnessed the raid of al-Muraysīʿ with the Messenger of God, and a man of the Anṣār killed him by mistake, thinking him a polytheist. Miqyas came to the Messenger of God, who ruled the blood-money for him against the killer's kin; he took it and converted, then attacked the killer of his brother and killed him, and fled as an apostate, saying:

It healed the soul that he lay in the open ground,his two garments dyed with the blood of his jugular veins.I took my vengeance on him by force and bore his blood-price,the lords of the Banū'l-Najjār, masters of Fāriʿ.I settled my blood-feud and attained my revenge,and I was the first to turn back from Islam.

ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib ﵁ killed al-Ḥuwayrith b. Nuqaydh b. Bujayr b. ʿAbd b. Quṣayy, whom the Prophet had ordered killed by whoever found him.

137Bakr b. al-Haytham told me, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī, who said: A singing-girl of Hilāl b. ʿAbd Allāh, who is Ibn Khaṭal al-Adramī of the Banū Taym, came to the Prophet in disguise, converted and swore allegiance, and he did not recognize her, so he did not harm her. And her other singing-girl was killed; the two used to sing satires on the Messenger of God. He said: And Ibn al-Zibaʿrā al-Sahmī converted before he could be caught, and praised the Messenger of God; he had made his blood lawful on the day of the conquest but did not harm him.

138Muḥammad b. al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Bazzāz told us: Hushaym told us: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ informed us, from al-Qāsim b. Rabīʿa, that the Messenger of God gave a sermon on the day of Mecca and said: "Praise be to God who fulfilled His promise, aided His army, and defeated the Confederates alone. Every distinction of the pre-Islamic period, every blood and claim, is placed beneath my feet, except the custodianship of the House and the giving of water to the pilgrims."

139Khalaf al-Bazzār told us: Ismāʿīl b. ʿAyyāsh told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from his elders, who said: On the day of the conquest of Mecca the Prophet said to Quraysh: "What do you think?" They said: "We think well and say well: a noble brother and son of a noble brother, and you have prevailed." He said: "Then I say as my brother Joseph ﵇ said: 'No blame on you today; God forgives you, and He is the most merciful of the merciful' (12:92). Every debt, property and distinction of the pre-Islamic period is beneath my feet, except the custodianship of the House and the giving of water to the pilgrims."

140Shaybān told us: Jarīr b.
