Ḥāzim told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr told us, who said: The Messenger of God said in his sermon: "Mecca is sacred between its two mountains; it was not lawful to anyone before me and will not be lawful to anyone after me, and it was lawful to me only for an hour of a day. Its grass is not to be cut, its thorn trees not felled, its game not startled, and its lost property not picked up except by one who will announce it or be announcing it." Al-ʿAbbās ﵀ said: "Except idhkhir, for it is for our goldsmiths, our blacksmiths and the purification of our houses." The Messenger of God said: "Except idhkhir."

141Yūsuf b. Mūsā al-Qaṭṭān told us: Jarīr b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that the Prophet said: "The grass of Mecca is not to be cut nor its trees felled." Al-ʿAbbās said: "Except idhkhir, for it is for the smiths and the purification of houses." So he gave permission for that.

142Shaybān told us: Abū Hilāl al-Rāsibī told us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: ʿUmar wanted to take the treasure of the Kaʿba and spend it in the cause of God. Ubayy b. Kaʿb al-Anṣārī said to him: "O commander of the faithful! Your two companions preceded you, and had this been a virtue they would have done it."

143ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us: Abū Muʿāwiya told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, who said: The Messenger of God said: "Mecca is sacred; the sale of its plots is not lawful, nor the rent of its houses."

144Muḥammad b. Ḥātim al-Marwazī told us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī told us, from Isrāʾīl, from Ibrāhīm b. Muhājir, from Yūsuf b. Māhak, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, shall I build you a shelter in Mecca to shade you from the sun?" He said: "It is only a resting-place for whoever gets there first."

145Khalaf b. Hishām al-Bazzār told us: Ismāʿīl told us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I read the letter of ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz forbidding renting out the houses of Mecca.

146Abū ʿUbayd told us: Ismāʿīl b. Jaʿfar told us, from Isrāʾīl, from Thuwayr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The whole sanctuary is a mosque.

147ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us: Isḥāq al-Azraq told us, from ʿAbd al-Malik b. Abī Sulaymān, who said: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to the governor of Mecca: "Do not let the people of Mecca take rent for the houses of Mecca, for it is not lawful for them."

148ʿUthmān b. Abī Shayba told us: Jarīr told us, from Yazīd b. Abī Ziyād, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Sābiṭ, regarding the words "equal are the resident therein and the visitor" (22:25): He said: The visitor is whoever comes from among the pilgrims and ʿumra-performers; they are equal in lodgings, lodging where they wish, except that no one is to be put out of his house.

149ʿUthmān told us: Jarīr told us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, about this verse: The people of Mecca and others are equal in lodgings.

150ʿUthmān and ʿAmr told us: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, that ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb said to the people of Mecca: "Do not put doors on your houses, so that the visitor may lodge where he wishes."

151ʿUthmān b. Abī Shayba and Bakr b. al-Haytham told us: Yaḥyā b. Ḍurays al-Rāzī told us, from Sufyān, from Abū Ḥuṣayn, who said: I said to Saʿīd b. Jubayr, while he was in Mecca: "I want to make iʿtikāf." He said: "You are a resident (ʿākif)." Then he recited "equal are the resident therein and the visitor."

152ʿUthmān told us: Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Muslim, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, regarding "equal are the resident therein and the visitor": He said: God's creatures in it are equal: the people of Mecca and others.

153Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, from al-Wāqidī, who said: Disputes over the rents of houses in Mecca were brought to Abū Bakr b. Muḥammad b. ʿAmr b. Ḥazm, and he would rule that rent was due from whoever had rented. This is the opinion of Mālik and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb. He said: Rabīʿa and Abū'l-Zinād said: There is no harm in eating the rent of Mecca's houses or selling its plots. Al-Wāqidī said: I saw Ibn Abī Dhiʾb receive the rent of his house in Mecca between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa.

Cairo page 51

Al-Layth b. Saʿd said: Whatever house is rented, its rent is lawful for its owner. As for open courtyards, lanes, forecourts and ruined plots, whoever gets there first may lodge in them without paying rent.

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Awdī informed me of the same from al-Shāfiʿī.

Sufyān b. Saʿīd al-Thawrī said: Renting out the houses of Mecca is forbidden. He was strict about this.

Al-Awzāʿī, Ibn Abī Laylā and Abū Ḥanīfa said: If one rents them out during the nights of the Hajj, the rent is void; if it is outside the nights of the Hajj, and the tenant is a neighbour (mujāwir) or otherwise, there is no harm.

Some of the companions of Abū Yūsuf said: Renting them out is entirely lawful; only in circumambulating the House are the resident and the visitor equal.

154 – al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad told us: ʿUbayd Allāh b. Mūsā told us, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. al-Musayyab, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad, that he saw no harm in the vegetables of Mecca, nor in the crops sown there , nor in anything people had grown there, whether tree or palm: that you may cut it and eat it and do with it as you wish.

He said: He disliked only what the soil of Mecca itself produced, of trees and the like, which people had not planted, except for the idhkhir (lemongrass).

Al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ said: Concession was also given for withered, dry, broken-off trees.

155 – Muḥammad b. ʿUmar al-Wāqidī said: Mālik and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said: Whether a person in iḥrām or one not in iḥrām cuts a tree in the Sanctuary, he has done wrong; if he was ignorant, he is taught and nothing is incumbent on him,

Cairo page 52

but if he knew and was deliberately defying the rule, he is punished and owes no compensation (qīma); and whoever cuts anything of it, there is no harm in his making use of it.

He said: Sufyān al-Thawrī and Abū Yūsuf said: For cutting a tree he owes its value, and he may not use it. That is also the opinion of Abū Ḥanīfa.

Mālik b. Anas and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said: There is no harm in taking ḍaghābīs (small cucumbers) and the tips of senna from the Sanctuary for medicine and for tooth-sticks.

Sufyān b. Saʿīd, Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf said: Whatever people have planted in the Sanctuary, or whatever is of the kind they plant, there is nothing on the one who cuts it; but whatever is of the kind people do not plant, the cutter owes its value.

Al-Wāqidī said: I asked al-Thawrī and Abū Yūsuf about a man who planted in the Sanctuary something people do not [normally] plant, and tended it until it grew for him: may he cut it? They said: Yes. I said: And if a tree of a kind people do not plant grows in his orchard without his having planted it? They said: He may do with it as he wishes.

156 – Muḥammad b. Saʿd related to me, from al-Wāqidī, who said: It was related to us that Ibn ʿUmar used to eat in Mecca vegetables that had been sown in the Sanctuary.

157 – Muḥammad b. Saʿd related to me: al-Wāqidī told me, from Muʿādh b. Muḥammad, who said: I saw on al-Zuhrī's table vegetables from the Sanctuary.

Abū Ḥanīfa said: A man in iḥrām may not let his camel graze in the Sanctuary, nor cut grass for it. This is also the opinion of Zufar.

Cairo page 53

Mālik, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, Sufyān, Abū Yūsuf and Ibn Abī Sabra said: There is no harm in grazing, but he may not cut grass.

Ibn Abī Laylā said: There is no harm in cutting grass.

158 – ʿAffān and al-ʿAbbās b. al-Walīd al-Narsī related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ziyād told us: Layth told us: ʿAṭāʾ saw no harm in the vegetables of the Sanctuary and what is sown in it, nor in a [cut] branch or a tooth-stick. He said: Mujāhid disliked it.

159 – He said: In the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ and of Abū Bakr, the Sacred Mosque had no surrounding wall. When ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb became caliph and the people multiplied, he enlarged the mosque; he bought houses, demolished them and added them to it. He demolished [the houses of] some of the mosque's neighbours who refused to sell, and deposited the prices for them until they took them later. He built a low wall around the mosque, below a man's height, and the lamps were placed on it.

When ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān became caliph he bought dwellings and enlarged the mosque with them, and took the dwellings of some people and deposited the prices for them. They cried out against him at the House. He said: What has emboldened you is my forbearance towards you and my gentleness with you. ʿUmar did the like of this to you and you accepted and were content. Then he ordered them to prison, until ʿAbd Allāh b. Khālid b. Asīd b. Abī l-ʿĪṣ spoke to him on their behalf and he released them.

It is said that ʿUthmān was the first to provide the mosque with porticoes (arwiqa), and he made them when he enlarged it.

160 – They said: In the time of Abraham ﵇ and of Jurhum and the ʿAmāliq, the door of the Kaʿba was at ground level, until Quraysh rebuilt it. Abū Ḥudhayfa b. al-Mughīra said: O people! Raise the door of the Kaʿba

Cairo page 54

so that no one can enter it except by a ladder; then only those whom you wish will enter, and if someone you dislike comes, you can throw him down and he will fall, as a deterrent to those behind him. Quraysh did so.

161 – He said: When ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr b. al-ʿAwwām fortified himself in the Sacred Mosque and sought refuge in it, while al-Ḥuṣayn b. Numayr al-Sakūnī was fighting him at the head of the Syrians, one day one of the men took fire on a piece of palm-fibre at the head of a spear. The wind was fierce, its sparks flew and caught on the hangings of the Kaʿba and burned them; its walls cracked and blackened. That was in the year 64. Then, when Yazīd b. Muʿāwiya died and al-Ḥuṣayn b. Numayr returned to Syria, Ibn al-Zubayr ordered the stones that had been hurled [by the catapults] and were in the mosque to be taken out. Then he demolished the Kaʿba and rebuilt it on its foundations, including the Ḥijr within it, and made two doors for it, set at ground level, one east and one west, so that one enters by one and leaves by the other. He had found the foundation of the Kaʿba joined to the Ḥijr. He sought only to restore it to the building of Abraham ﵇ according to what ʿĀʾisha, Mother of the Believers, had told him from the Prophet ﷺ.

He put plates of gold on its door and made its keys of gold.

When al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf, on behalf of ʿAbd al-Malik b. Marwān, fought him and killed him, ʿAbd al-Malik wrote to him ordering him to rebuild the Kaʿba and the Sacred Mosque. The stones had loosened the Kaʿba, so al-Ḥajjāj demolished it and rebuilt it, returning it to the construction of Quraysh and taking the Ḥijr out. ʿAbd al-Malik afterwards used to say: I wish I had left Ibn al-Zubayr to bear what he bore regarding the Kaʿba and its construction.

162 – They said: In the Jāhiliyya the covering of the Kaʿba was of leather mats and mail-hoods. The Messenger of God ﷺ covered it with Yemeni cloths; then ʿUmar and ʿUthmān ﵃ covered it with Coptic linen (qubāṭī); then Yazīd b. Muʿāwiya covered it with Khusrawānī brocade; and

Cairo page 55

Ibn al-Zubayr, and al-Ḥajjāj after him, covered it with brocade. The Banū Umayya in some of their days covered it with the robes (ḥulal) which the people of Najrān used to pay, requiring them to make them fine, with brocade over them.

Then al-Walīd b. ʿAbd al-Malik enlarged the Sacred Mosque and had columns of stone, marble and mosaic carried to it.

163 – Al-Wāqidī said: When the caliphate of the Commander of the Faithful al-Manṣūr ﵀ came, he enlarged the mosque and built it; that was in the year 139.

164 – ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Madāʾinī said: al-Mahdī appointed Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAbbās over Mecca, Medina and al-Yamāma, and he enlarged the two mosques of Mecca and Medina and built them.

The Commander of the Faithful al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh Jaʿfar b. Abī Isḥāq al-Muʿtaṣim bi-llāh b. al-Rashīd Hārūn b. al-Mahdī, may God's good pleasure be upon them, renewed the marble of the Kaʿba and girded its base with silver, and covered all its walls and its ceiling with gold; no one before him had done that. He also clothed its pillars in brocade.

Chapter 8

The wells of Mecca

Account of the Wells of Mecca

165 – They said: Before Quṣayy united them and before they entered Mecca, Quraysh drank from cisterns and reservoirs on mountaintops, and from a well that Luʾayy b. Ghālib dug outside the Sanctuary called al-Yasīra, and from a well that Murra b. Kaʿb dug called al-Rawī, which is on the side nearest ʿArafa.

Then Kilāb b. Murra dug Khumm and Rumm, and al-Jafr on the outskirts of Mecca.

Then Quṣayy b. Kilāb dug a well which he named al-ʿAjūl and set up a drinking-station (siqāya). Concerning it one of the pilgrims' rajaz-poets said:

We water at al-ʿAjūl, then we depart,before the pilgrims' return from every horizon.Quṣayy has fulfilled and spoken true,with filling for the people and a draught for the evening-drinkers.

Later, after Quṣayy's death, a man of the Banū Naṣr b. Muʿāwiya fell into al-ʿAjūl and it was put out of use.

Hāshim b. ʿAbd Manāf dug Badhar, which is at al-Khandama at the mouth of the pass of Abū Ṭālib. Hāshim also dug Sajla, which Asad b. Hāshim gave to ʿAdī b. Nawfal b. ʿAbd Manāf b. al-Muṭʿim; or it is said he bought it from him; and it is said that ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib gave it to him when he dug Zamzam and water became plentiful in Mecca. Khālida bint Hāshim said:

We gave to ʿAdī Sajla,in soil of rich, easy-flowing water,that waters the pilgrims draught after draught.

Sajla has since been absorbed into the mosque.

ʿAbd Shams b. ʿAbd Manāf dug al-Ṭuwā, which is at the upper part of Mecca, and also dug al-Jafr for himself.

Cairo page 57

Maymūn b. al-Ḥaḍramī, an ally of the Banū ʿAbd Shams b. ʿAbd Manāf, dug his well. It was the last well dug in Mecca in the Jāhiliyya, and beside it is the grave of the Commander of the Faithful al-Manṣūr ﵀. Al-Ḥaḍramī's name was ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿImād.

ʿAbd Shams also dug two wells and named them Khumm and Rumm, after the names Kilāb b. Murra gave to his two wells. Khumm is near al-Radm; Rumm is by the house of Khadīja bint Khuwaylid. ʿAbd Shams said:

I dug Khumm and I dug Rummuntil I see glory complete for us.

Subayʿa bint ʿAbd Shams said of al-Ṭuwā:

Al-Ṭuwā — when you drink its water —is the rain-cloud's downpour in sweetness and clarity.

The Banū Asad b. ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā b. Quṣayy dug Shufayya, the well of the Banū Asad. Al-Ḥuwayrith b. Asad said:

The water of Shufayya is like cloud-water,its water is not stale or foul.

The Banū ʿAbd al-Dār b. Quṣayy dug Umm Aḥrād. Umayma bint ʿUmayla b. al-Sabbāq b. ʿAbd al-Dār said:

We dug the sea, Umm Aḥrād,not like the meagre, sparse Badhar.

Ṣafiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib answered her:

We dug Badhar,which waters the greatest pilgrimage,those coming and going.Umm Aḥrād is evil:locusts and ants are in it,and filth not to be mentioned.

The Banū Jumaḥ dug al-Sunbula, the well of Khalaf b. Wahb al-Jumaḥī. One of them said:

We dug al-Sunbula for the pilgrims,a downpour of cloud which the Lord of Majesty sent down.

Cairo page 58

The Banū Sahm dug al-Ghamr, the well of al-ʿĀṣī b. Wāʾil. One of them said:

We dug al-Ghamr for the pilgrims,it gushes water, what a gushing!

Ibn al-Kalbī said: Ibn al-Rabʿī said it.

The Banū ʿAdī dug al-Ḥafīr, and their poet said:

We dug our well al-Ḥafīr,a sea whose water boils up abundantly.

The Banū Makhzūm dug al-Suqyā, the well of Hishām b. al-Mughīra b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar b. Makhzūm.

The Banū Taym dug al-Thurayyā, the well of ʿAbd Allāh b. Judʿān b. ʿAmr b. Kaʿb b. Saʿd b. Taym.

The Banū ʿĀmir b. Luʾayy dug al-Naqʿ.

166 – They said: Jubayr b. Muṭʿim had a well, the well of the Banū Nawfal, which was recently absorbed into the Dār al-Qawārīr that Ḥammād al-Barbarī built in the caliphate of the Commander of the Faithful Hārūn al-Rashīd.

ʿAqīl b. Abī Ṭālib had dug a well in the Jāhiliyya, which is in the house of Ibn Yūsuf.

Al-Aswad b. Abī l-Bakhtarī b. Hāshim b. al-Ḥārith b. Asad b. ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā had a well at Bāb al-Aswad near the grain-sellers, which was absorbed into the mosque.

The well of ʿIkrima, named after ʿIkrima b. Khālid b. al-ʿĀṣī b. Hāshim b. al-Mughīra.

The well of ʿAmr, named after ʿAmr b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣafwān b. Umayya b. Khalaf al-Jumaḥī; likewise the ravine of ʿAmr al-Ṭalūb in lower Mecca belonged to ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣafwān.

The well of Ḥuwayṭib, named after Ḥuwayṭib b. ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā b. Abī Qays of the Banū ʿĀmir b. Luʾayy; it is in the courtyard of his house in the middle of the valley.

The well of Abū Mūsā belonged to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, at al-Muʿallā.

Cairo page 59

The well of Shūdhab, named after Shūdhab, freedman of Muʿāwiya; it has been absorbed into the mosque. It is said that Shūdhab was a freedman of Ṭāriq b. ʿAlqama b. ʿUrayj b. Judhayma al-Kinānī; and it is said he was a freedman of Nāfiʿ b. ʿAlqama b. Ṣafwān b. Umayya b. Muḥrith b. Khumal b. Shaqq al-Kinānī, maternal uncle of Marwān b. al-Ḥakam b. Abī l-ʿĀṣī b. Umayya.

The well of Bakkār, named after a man from Iraq who settled in Mecca; it is at Dhū Ṭuwā.

The well of Wardān, named after Wardān, freedman of al-Sāʾib b. Abī Wadāʿa b. Ḍubayra al-Sahmī.

The drinking-station of Sirāj at Fakhkh belonged to Sirāj, a freedman of the Banū Hāshim.

The well of al-Aswad, named after al-Aswad b. Sufyān b. ʿAbd al-Asad b. Hilāl b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar b. Makhzūm; it is near the well of Khāliṣa, freedwoman of the Commander of the Faithful al-Mahdī.

Al-Burūd at Fakhkh belonged to Mukhtarish al-Kaʿbī of Khuzāʿa.

167 – Ibn al-Kalbī said: The owner of the house of Ibn ʿAlqama in Mecca was Ṭāriq b. ʿAlqama b. ʿUrayj b. Judhayma al-Kinānī.

168 – Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā, ʿAbd al-Malik b. Qurayb al-Aṣmaʿī and others said: The orchard of Ibn ʿĀmir belonged to ʿUmar b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. Maʿmar b. ʿUthmān b. ʿAmr b. Kaʿb b. Taym b. Murra b. Kaʿb b. Luʾayy, but people have erred about it and said "Ibn ʿĀmir's orchard" and "the orchard of the Banū ʿĀmir." It is in truth the orchard of Ibn Maʿmar. Some say it is named after Ibn ʿĀmir al-Ḥaḍramī, and others say after Ibn ʿĀmir b. Kurayz. That is conjecture and guesswork.

Cairo page 60

169 – Muṣʿab b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Zubayrī related to me: In the Jāhiliyya Mecca was called Ṣalāḥ. Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb al-Ḥaḍramī said:

Abū Maṭar, come to Ṣalāḥ,that the drinking-companions of Quraysh may suffice you,and settle in a land long mighty,and be safe from any lord of an army reaching you.

170 – Al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām al-Kalbī related to me: Some men of Kinda wrote to my father asking about the prison of Ibn Sibāʿ in Medina, to whom it was attributed, and about the story of the Dār al-Nadwa, the Dār al-ʿAjala and the Dār al-Qawārīr in Mecca. He wrote back to him:

As for the prison of Ibn Sibāʿ, it was a house belonging to ʿAbd Allāh b. Sibāʿ b. ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā b. Nuḍla b. ʿAmr b. Ghubshān al-Khuzāʿī. Sibāʿ was called Abū Niyār, and his mother was a midwife in Mecca. Ḥamza b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib challenged him at Uḥud, saying to him: Come to me, son of the cutter of clitorises! Then he killed him and bent over him to take his coat of mail, whereupon Waḥshī struck him with his spear. The mother of Ṭurayḥ b. Ismāʿīl al-Thaqafī the poet was a daughter of ʿAbd Allāh b. Sibāʿ, an ally of the Banū Zuhra.

As for the Dār al-Nadwa, Quṣayy b. Kilāb built it. They used to gather to him there and affairs were settled in it. Thereafter Quraysh would gather in it to consult about their wars and affairs, to tie banners, and to marry off whoever wished to marry. It was the first house built in Mecca of the houses of Quraysh.

Then the Dār al-ʿAjala, which is the house of Saʿīd b. Saʿd b. Sahm. The Banū Sahm claim it was built before the Dār al-Nadwa, but that is false.

The Dār al-Nadwa remained with the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār b. Quṣayy until ʿIkrima b. ʿĀmir b. Hāshim b. ʿAbd Manāf b. ʿAbd al-Dār b. Quṣayy sold it to Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān, who made it the governor's residence.

As for the Dār al-Qawārīr, it belonged to ʿUtba b. Rabīʿa b. ʿAbd Shams b. ʿAbd Manāf. Then it passed to al-ʿAbbās b. ʿUtba b. Abī Lahab b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and later it came to belong to the mother of Jaʿfar, Zubayda bint Abī l-Faḍl b. al-Manṣūr, Commander of the Faithful.

Cairo page 61

Some of its floors and walls were fitted with something of glass (qawārīr), hence "the House of Glass." Ḥammād al-Barbarī built it in the caliphate of Hārūn al-Rashīd, Commander of the Faithful ﵀.

171 – Hishām b. Muḥammad al-Kalbī said: ʿAmr b. Muḍāḍ al-Jurhumī fought a man of Jurhum called al-Sumaydaʿ. ʿAmr went out in his weapons, clattering, so the place he went out from was named Quʿayqiʿān. Al-Sumaydaʿ went out with his horses bearing bells on their necks (ajyād), so the place he went out from was named Ajyād. Ibn al-Kalbī said: It is also said that he went out with fine horses (jiyād) bearing marks, hence the place was named Ajyād. Most of the people of Mecca say Jiyād al-Ṣaghīr and Jiyād al-Kabīr.

172 – al-Walīd b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from Muḥammad b. ʿUmar al-Aslamī, from Kathīr b. ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: We came with ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb on his ʿumra in the year 17, and the people of the watering-places on the road spoke to him about building dwellings between Mecca and Medina, which had not existed before. He permitted them, stipulating that the wayfarer has the prior right to water and shade.

Cairo page 62

Chapter 9

The floods of Mecca

Account of the Floods of Mecca

173 – al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām told us, from his father Hishām b. Muḥammad, from Ibn Kharbūz al-Makkī and others, who said: There were four floods in Mecca. Among them was the flood of Umm Nahshal, in the time of ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb. The flood came on until it entered the mosque from the upper part of Mecca, so ʿUmar built both dams: the upper one, between the house of Dabba – that is, ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith b. Nawfal b. al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib b. ʿAbd Manāf, who governed Basra during the strife of Ibn al-Zubayr, its people having agreed on him – and the house of Abān b. ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān; and the lower one at the donkey-drivers' quarter, which is known as the dam of Āl Usayd. The flood was thereby turned back from the Sacred Mosque.

He said: Umm Nahshal bint ʿUbayda b. Saʿīd b. al-ʿĀṣī b. Umayya was carried off by the flood from the upper part of Mecca, and it was named after her.

Among them also is the flood of al-Juḥāf (or al-Jurāf) in the year 80, in the time of ʿAbd al-Malik b. Marwān. It struck the pilgrims on Monday morning and carried them off with their baggage, and surrounded the Kaʿba. The poet said:

Ghassān never saw a day like Monday,more grief-stricken, more tearful of eye,when the flood carried off the people of the two cities,and the veiled women came out running scattered in the two mountains, climbing.

ʿAbd al-Malik wrote to ʿAbd Allāh b. Sufyān al-Makhzūmī, his governor over Mecca – or it is said his governor then was al-Ḥārith b. Khālid al-Makhzūmī the poet – ordering him to build revetments (ḍafāʾir) for the houses fronting the valley and for the mosque, and to build a dam at the mouths of the lanes to protect people's houses. He sent a Christian man to do this, who made the revetments and built the dam known as the Dam of the Banū Qurād, also known as that of the Banū Jumaḥ, and dams were made in lower Mecca. The poet said:

I shall master a tear and let another flowwhen I pass the dam of the Banū Qurād.

Cairo page 63

Among them also is the flood called al-Mukhabbal ("the Deranging"): in its days the people suffered sickness in their bodies and impairment (khabal) in their tongues, so it was named al-Mukhabbal.

Among them also is a flood that came afterwards in the caliphate of Hishām b. ʿAbd al-Malik, in the year 120, known as the flood of Abū Shākir, that is, Maslama b. Hishām, who was in charge of the pilgrimage that year, so it was named after him.

He said: The flood of the valley of Mecca comes from a place known as the lote-tree of ʿAttāb b. Asīd b. Abī l-ʿĪṣ.

ʿAbbās b. Hishām said: In the caliphate of al-Maʾmūn ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Rashīd ﵀ there was a great flood whose water reached nearly to the Ḥijr.

174 – al-ʿAbbās related to me: my father related to me, from his father Muḥammad b. al-Sāʾib al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from ʿIkrima, who said: Some of the landmarks of the Sanctuary became effaced in the time of Muʿāwiya b. Abī Sufyān. He wrote to Marwān b. al-Ḥakam, his governor over Medina, ordering him, if Kurz b. ʿAlqama al-Khuzāʿī were alive, to charge him with re-establishing the landmarks of the Sanctuary because of his knowledge of them. He was long-lived. He set them up on them, and those are the sites of the boundary-markers today.

Cairo page 64

Al-Kalbī said: This is Kurz b. ʿAlqama b. Hilāl b. Jurayba b. ʿAbd Nahm b. Ḥulayl b. Ḥabashiyya al-Khuzāʿī. He is the one who followed the Prophet's tracks ﷺ until he reached the cave in which he and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq hid when he intended the emigration to Medina; he saw spider's web over it, and saw below it the footprint of the Messenger of God ﷺ and recognized it and said: This is the foot of Muḥammad ﷺ and here the trail ends.

Cairo page 65

Chapter 10

Al-Ṭāʾif

175 – He said: When Hawāzin was defeated on the day of Ḥunayn and Durayd b. al-Ṣimma was killed, their routed remnant came to Awṭās. The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Abū ʿĀmir al-Ashʿarī against them and he was killed; Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh b. Qays al-Ashʿarī took charge of the men. The Muslims advanced on Awṭās. When Mālik b. ʿAwf b. Saʿd, of the Banū Dahmān b. Naṣr b. Muʿāwiya b. Bakr b. Hawāzin – who was the chief of Hawāzin that day – saw this, he fled to al-Ṭāʾif and found its people prepared for a siege: they had repaired their fortress and stored provisions in it. He stayed there. The Messenger of God ﷺ marched with the Muslims until he encamped at al-Ṭāʾif. Thaqīf pelted them with stones and arrows, and the Messenger of God ﷺ set up a catapult (manjanīq) against their fortress. The Muslims had a dabbāba (siege-shed) made of cowhides, but Thaqīf threw heated iron spikes on it and burned it, and the Muslims beneath it were hit. The Messenger of God's siege of al-Ṭāʾif lasted fifteen nights. His campaign against it was in Shawwāl of the year 8.

176 – They said: Some of the slaves of the people of al-Ṭāʾif came down to the Messenger of God ﷺ among them Abū Bakra b. Masrūḥ, freedman of the Messenger of God ﷺ whose name was Nufayʿ; and among them al-Azraq, to whom the Azāriqa are attributed, who was a Byzantine slave, a blacksmith, and the father of Nāfiʿ b. al-Azraq the Khārijite. They were freed by their coming down. It is said that Nāfiʿ b. al-Azraq the Khārijite was of the Banū Ḥanīfa, and that the al-Azraq who came down from al-Ṭāʾif was someone else.

Then the Messenger of God ﷺ withdrew to al-Jiʿrāna to divide the captives and spoils of Ḥunayn. Thaqīf feared he would return to them, so they sent him their delegation, and he made peace with them on

Cairo page 66

the terms that they would become Muslim and he would leave them what they possessed of their property and buried treasure (rikāz), stipulating that they not practise usury nor drink wine – they had been people of usury. He wrote them a document.

He said: Al-Ṭāʾif was called Wajj; when it was fortified and its wall built, it was called al-Ṭāʾif.

177 – al-Madāʾinī related to me, from Abū Ismāʿīl al-Ṭāʾifī, from his father, from elders of the people of al-Ṭāʾif, who said: In the district (mikhlāf) of al-Ṭāʾif there was a group of Jews who had been expelled from Yemen and Yathrib; they settled there for trade, and the poll-tax was imposed on them. From some of them Muʿāwiya bought his estates in al-Ṭāʾif.

178 – They said: al-ʿAbbās b. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib ﵀ had land in al-Ṭāʾif from which raisins were carried to be steeped in the pilgrims' drinking-station. Quraysh generally owned properties in al-Ṭāʾif, which they would come to from Mecca and tend. When Mecca was conquered and its people became Muslim, Thaqīf coveted them; but when al-Ṭāʾif was conquered they were left in the hands of the Meccans, and the land of al-Ṭāʾif became a mikhlāf of the makhālīf of Mecca.

179 – They said: On the day of al-Ṭāʾif the eye of Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb was struck.

180 – al-Walīd b. Ṣāliḥ told us: al-Wāqidī told us, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Zuhrī, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿAttāb b. Asīd, that the Messenger of God ﷺ ordered that the grapes of Thaqīf be estimated (takhrīṣ) like dates, and that their zakāt then be taken in raisins as the zakāt of dates is paid.

Al-Wāqidī said: Abū Ḥanīfa said: They are not estimated; rather, when they are laid on the ground the ṣadaqa is taken from the small amount of it

Cairo page 67

and the large . Yaʿqūb said: When it is laid on the ground and its measure reaches five awsuq, it is subject to zakāt, the tithe or half-tithe. That is the opinion of Sufyān b. Saʿīd al-Thawrī. The wasq is sixty ṣāʿs.

Mālik b. Anas and Ibn Abī Dhiʾb said: The sunna is that zakāt be taken from it by estimation as dates are taken from the palm.

181 – Shaybān b. Abī Shayba told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us: Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd told us, from ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb, that a governor of ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ over al-Ṭāʾif wrote to him: The honey-keepers do not deliver to us what they used to deliver to the Messenger of God ﷺ namely one skin out of every ten skins. ʿUmar wrote back to him: If they do so, protect their valleys for them [as pasture-reserves]; otherwise, do not protect them.

182 – ʿAmr b. Muḥammad al-Nāqid told us: Ismāʿīl b. Ibrāhīm told us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Isḥāq, from his father, from his grandfather, from ʿUmar, that he imposed the tithe on honey.

183 – Dāwūd b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, judge of al-Raqqa, told us, from Marwān b. Shujāʿ, from Khuṣayf, from ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that he wrote to his governors over Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif: There is ṣadaqa on beehives (khalāyā); take it from them. He said: The khalāyā are the kawāʾir.

184 – Al-Wāqidī said: It is related from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: There is no ṣadaqa on beehives.

Cairo page 68

Mālik and al-Thawrī said: There is no zakāt on honey, however much, and this is also al-Shāfiʿī's view.

Abū Ḥanīfa said: On honey, small or large, if it is on tithe-land, the tithe is due; if it is on kharāj land, nothing is due, because zakāt and kharāj are not combined on one man.

185 – Al-Wāqidī said: al-Qāsim b. Maʿn and Yaʿqūb told me, from Abū Ḥanīfa, that he said regarding honey on the land of a dhimmī, where it is of the tithe-lands: there is no tithe on it, and his land bears kharāj. If it is on the land of a Taghlibī, a fifth is taken from it. Zufar's view is like Abū Ḥanīfa's.

Abū Yūsuf said: If the honey is on kharāj land, nothing is due; if it is on tithe-land, then on every ten raṭls one raṭl. Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan said: There is no ṣadaqa on less than five faraqs; and this is also the view of Ibn Abī Dhiʾb.

186 – Khālid b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṭaḥḥān related, from Ibn Abī Laylā, that he said: If it is on kharāj or tithe land, then on every ten raṭls one raṭl. That is also the view of al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayy.

187 – Abū ʿUbayd told me: Muḥammad b. Kathīr told us, from al-Awzāʿī, from al-Zuhrī, who said: On every ten skins, one skin.

Cairo page 69

188 – al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Ḥumayd al-Ruʾāsī told us, from Jaʿfar b. Nujayḥ al-Madīnī, from Bishr b. ʿĀṣim and ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Aws, that Sufyān b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Thaqafī, who was ʿUmar's governor over al-Ṭāʾif, wrote to ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ mentioning that he had walled gardens containing vines and also peaches and pomegranates, which yielded many times more produce than the vines, and asked his instructions about the tithe. He said: ʿUmar wrote back to him: There is no tithe on them.

Yaḥyā b. Ādam said: This is the view of Sufyān b. Saʿīd; I heard him say: There is no ṣadaqa in anything the earth produces except four things: wheat, barley, dates and raisins, once each reaches five awsuq.

He said: Abū Ḥanīfa said: On what tithe-land produces, the tithe is due, even a bundle of vegetables. And this is Zufar's view.

Mālik, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb and Yaʿqūb said: There is no ṣadaqa on vegetables and the like. They said: There is no ṣadaqa on less than five awsuq of wheat, barley, sorghum, sult (naked barley), zuwān (darnel), dates, raisins, rice, sesame, julubbān (vetch), and the kinds of grains that are measured and stored, together with lentils, cowpeas, chickpeas, mung beans and millet; but when they reach five awsuq, ṣadaqa is due on them.

Al-Wāqidī said: This is the view of Rabīʿa b. Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.

Al-Zuhrī said: Spices and all pulses (qaṭānī) are subject to zakāt.

Mālik said: Nothing is due on the pear, nor on the firsik – which is the peach (khawkh) – nor on the pomegranate and all kinds of fresh fruit by way of ṣadaqa. That is also the view of Ibn Abī Laylā.

Abū Yūsuf said: Ṣadaqa is due only on what

Cairo page 70

the qafīz falls upon and measuring applies to.

Abū l-Zinād, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb and Ibn Abī Sabra said: Nothing is due on greens and fruits by way of ṣadaqa; rather, the ṣadaqa is on their price at the moment they are sold.

189 – ʿAbbās b. Hishām related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed ʿUthmān b. Abī l-ʿĀṣī al-Thaqafī over al-Ṭāʾif.

Cairo page 71

Chapter 11

Tabāla and Jurash

190 – Bakr b. al-Haytham related to me, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, who said: The people of Tabāla and Jurash became Muslim without fighting. The Messenger of God ﷺ confirmed them in what they had become Muslim upon, and imposed on every adult (ḥālim) among the People of the Book in the two places one dinar, stipulating hospitality for the Muslims, and appointed Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb over Jurash.

Chapter 12

Tabūk, Ayla, Adhruḥ, Maqnā and al-Jarbāʾ

191 – They said: The Messenger of God ﷺ set out for Tabūk, on the border of Syria, to fight those of the Byzantines, ʿĀmila, Lakhm, Judhām and others who, it had reached him, had gathered against him. That was in the year 9 of the Hijra. He met with no plot. He stayed at Tabūk some days, and its people made peace with him on payment of the poll-tax. While he was there Yuḥanna b. Ruʾba, lord of Ayla, came to him, and he made peace with him on the basis that he would impose on every adult in his land one dinar per year, which came to three hundred dinars. He stipulated that they provide hospitality to Muslims passing through them, and he wrote them a document that they be protected and defended.

192 – Muḥammad b. Saʿd related to me: al-Wāqidī told us, from Khālid b. Rabīʿa, from Ṭalḥa al-Aylī, that ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz would not increase [the levy] on the people of Ayla beyond three hundred dinars. The Messenger of God ﷺ made peace with the people of Adhruḥ for one hundred dinars every Rajab. He made peace with the people of al-Jarbāʾ on the poll-tax and wrote them a document. And he made peace with the people of Maqnā on a quarter of their ʿurūk – the ʿurūk are wood on which game is hunted [i.e., fishing-weirs/traps] –

Cairo page 72

and a quarter of their riding-beasts and coats of mail, and a quarter of their fruits; they were Jews.

One of the people of Egypt informed me that he saw their document with his own eyes, on a red skin, its writing effaced; he copied it and dictated to me from his copy:

"In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. From Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, to the Banū Ḥabība and the people of Maqnā. Peace be upon you. It has been revealed to me that you are returning to your village. So when this letter of mine reaches you, you are safe, and you have the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger. The Messenger of God has forgiven you your sins and every blood-debt you were pursued for. You have no partner in your village except the Messenger of God or the messenger of the Messenger of God. No wrong or aggression shall be done to you. The Messenger of God ﷺ shields you from what he shields himself. The Messenger of God has your weapons-gear (bizza), your slaves, the riding-beasts and the coats of mail, except what the Messenger of God or the messenger of the Messenger of God excuses. After that, you owe a quarter of what your palms produce, a quarter of what your ʿurūk catch, and a quarter of what your women spin. After that you are quit, and the Messenger of God ﷺ has lifted from you all poll-tax and forced labour. If you hear and obey, it is for the Messenger of God to honour your noble, to pardon your wrongdoer; and whoever of the Muslims counsels good regarding the Banū Ḥabība and the people of Maqnā, it is better for him, and whoever brings them evil, it is worse for him. You shall have no governor except from yourselves or from the household of the Messenger of God ﷺ. ʿAlī b. Abū Ṭālib wrote it, in the year 9." (1)

(1) In the margin of manuscript A is the following: The one hoping for the mercy of his Lord, Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. ʿAsākir, says: This is how it appears vocalized in the manuscript, in the form at the end of the book: "and ʿAlī b. Abū Ṭālib wrote it in the year 9." So too is the report about the whole set of documents held by the Jews, attributed to the handwriting of ʿAlī, may God honour his face. In this there is room for reflection by one of understanding who considers it: it will become clear to him that this document is fabricated, and the proof is twofold. First, ʿAlī, may God honour his face, is the one who originated speech on the science of grammar, fearing the mixing of the speech of the Arabs with the speech of the Nabaṭ; he would not have feared something and then adopted what leads to confusion. Second, the Messenger of God's peace with the people of Maqnā took place only during the Tabūk expedition, as stated in this document itself, and there is no disagreement that ʿAlī was not with the Prophet ﷺ on the Tabūk expedition; so how is this document ascribed to him? This is sufficient.

Cairo page 73

Chapter 13

Dūmat al-Jandal

193 – He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Khālid b. al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī to Ukaydir b. ʿAbd al-Malik al-Kindī, then al-Sakūnī, at Dūmat al-Jandal. He took him captive and killed his brother and stripped him of a brocade tunic woven with gold, and brought Ukaydir to the Prophet ﷺ; he became Muslim, and the Prophet wrote for him and for the people of Dūma a document, whose text is:

"This is a document from Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, to Ukaydir, when he responded to Islam and renounced the rivals [to God] and the idols, and to the people of Dūma. To us belong the open lands (ḍāḥiya) of the shallow waters (ḍaḥl), the wastelands (būr), the uncharted lands (maʿāmī), the untrodden lands (aghfāl), the coats of mail and the weapons, the hoofed animals (ḥāfir) and the fortress; and to you belong the ḍāmina of the palm-groves and the running water (maʿīn) of the cultivated land. Your pasturing herd shall not be diverted (lā tuʿdal), your solitary animal (fāridatukum) shall not be counted [apart], and no herbage shall be barred to you. You shall perform prayer at its time and give zakāt in due measure. Upon you for this is the covenant of God and the pledge, and for you is truthfulness and fidelity. God and those of the Muslims present are witnesses."

Ḍāḥī means what is exposed; ḍaḥl is shallow water; būr is land that has not been brought out [into cultivation] and not worked; maʿāmī is unknown land; aghfāl is land with no traces in it; ḥalaqa means coats of mail; ḥāfir means horses, pack-horses, mules and donkeys; ḥiṣn is their fortress; ḍāmina is the palms that are with them in the fortress; and maʿīn is visible, permanent water.

His phrase "lā tuʿdal sāriḥatukum" [here glossed] "lā tuʿdal māshiyatukum" means: we will not take zakāt from it except in its pastures and its places, and we will not gather it; and his phrase "lā tuʿadd fāridatukum" means: the solitary animal is not joined to others and then the whole assessed, so as to combine what is separate.

194 – al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām al-Kalbī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Khālid b. al-Walīd to Ukaydir, who brought him to him; he became Muslim and [the Prophet] wrote him a document. When the Prophet ﷺ was taken [in death],

Cairo page 74

he withheld the ṣadaqa, broke the covenant, left Dūmat al-Jandal and joined al-Ḥīra, where he built a structure which he called Dūma, after Dūmat al-Jandal. His brother Ḥurayth b. ʿAbd al-Malik became Muslim, [retaining] what was in his hands, and that was left to him. Suwayd b. Shubayb al-Kalbī then said:

Let no people feel secure from the stumbling of their grandfathers,as the howdahs of Akdar departed from Khabt.

He said: Yazīd b. Muʿāwiya married the daughter of Ḥurayth, Ukaydir's brother.

Al-ʿAbbās said: My father informed me, from ʿAwāna b. al-Ḥakam, that Abū Bakr wrote to Khālid b. al-Walīd, who was at ʿAyn al-Tamr, ordering him to march against Ukaydir. He marched against him, killed him and conquered Dūma. [Ukaydir] had left it after the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ then returned to it; when Khālid killed him, he [Khālid] went on to Syria.

195 – Al-Wāqidī said: When Khālid set out from Iraq for Syria he passed Dūmat al-Jandal and conquered it, and took captives; among those captured from it was Laylā bint al-Jūdī al-Ghassānī. It is said she was taken in a camp of Ghassān , seized by his cavalry. Bint al-Jūdī is the one whom ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq loved and of whom he said:

I remembered Laylā while al-Samāwa lay between us,and what has the daughter of al-Jūdī, Laylā, to do with me?

She became his and he married her, and she so dominated him that he turned away from all his other wives. Then she fell gravely ill and her looks changed, so he came to dislike her. It was said to him: Give her a parting gift and return her to her people. He did.

Al-Wāqidī said: The Prophet ﷺ raided Dūmat al-Jandal in the year 5 and met no plot; and he sent Khālid b. al-Walīd to Ukaydir in Shawwāl of the year 9, twenty months after Khālid b. al-Walīd's conversion.

Cairo page 75

196 – I heard some of the people of al-Ḥīra mention that Ukaydir and his brothers used to dwell at Dūmat al-Ḥīra. They used to visit their maternal uncles of Kalb and stay abroad with them. While they were with them, out hunting, a ruined city appeared before them, of which nothing remained but some walls; it had been built of rock (jandal). They rebuilt it, planted olives and other things in it, and named it Dūmat al-Ḥīra.

197 – ʿAmr b. Muḥammad al-Nāqid related to me, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb al-Miṣrī, from Yūnus al-Aylī, from al-Zuhrī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Khālid b. al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra to the people of Dūmat al-Jandal. They were of the worshippers of al-Kūfa (?). He captured Ukaydir, their chief, and settled with him on the poll-tax.

Cairo page 76

Chapter 14

The peace treaty of Najrān

198 – Bakr b. al-Haytham related to me: ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from al-Layth b. Saʿd, from Yūnus b. Yazīd al-Aylī, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Al-Sayyid and al-ʿĀqib, the two delegates of the people of Najrān of Yemen, came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and asked him for peace. He made peace with them on behalf of the people of Najrān for two thousand ḥullas: two thousand in Ṣafar and one thousand in Rajab [sic: the text reads "2,000 in Ṣafar and 1,000 in Rajab"], the price of each ḥulla being an ūqiyya, the ūqiyya being forty dirhams in weight. If they paid a ḥulla worth more than an ūqiyya, the excess was credited to them; if they paid it worth less than an ūqiyya, the shortfall was taken from them. And whatever weapons, horses, mounts or goods they gave would be taken at their value in set-off against the ḥullas; and they were to host the messengers of the Messenger of God ﷺ for a month or less and not detain them beyond a month; and they were to lend thirty coats of mail, thirty horses and thirty camels if there was a plot in Yemen, and whatever of those loans perished the messengers were responsible for until they returned it. He gave them the protection of God and His covenant, that they not be tempted away from their religion and their ranks within it, nor be mustered [for military levy] nor tithed. He stipulated that they not consume usury nor deal in it.

199 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: Wakīʿ told us: Mubārak b. Fuḍāla told us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: Two monks of Najrān came to the Prophet ﷺ and he offered them Islam. They said: We became Muslim before you. He said: You lie. Three things keep you from Islam: your eating pork, your worshipping the cross, and your saying God has a son. They said: Then who is the father of Jesus? – Al-Ḥasan said: He ﷺ would not hasten until his Lord commanded him – so God Almighty revealed: "This We recite to you of the signs and the wise Reminder. Indeed the likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him 'Be,' and he was" – up to His words "the liars" (1).

Cairo page 77

The Messenger of God ﷺ recited it to them, then called them to mubāhala (mutual imprecation), taking by the hand Fāṭima, al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn. One said to his companion: Go up the mountain and do not engage in mubāhala with him, for if you do, you will earn the curse. He said: What do you think? He said: I think we should give him the tribute and not engage in mubāhala with him.

200 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: I took a copy of the letter of the Messenger of God ﷺ to the people of Najrān from the book of a man, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ ﵀ and it is:

"In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. This is what the Prophet, the Messenger of God Muḥammad, wrote for Najrān, when he had authority (ḥukūma) over them, over every fruit, yellow, white and black [wares], and slaves; he showed favour to them and left that for two thousand ḥullas, the ḥullas of ounces (awāqī): in every Rajab a thousand ḥullas and in every Ṣafar a thousand ḥullas. Each ḥulla is an ounce, and whatever the ḥullas of tribute exceed or fall short of the ounces is by reckoning; whatever they pay of coat of mail, horse, mount or goods is taken from them by reckoning. Najrān owes the lodging of my messengers for a month or less, and my messengers are not to be detained beyond a month. They owe the loan of thirty coats of mail, thirty horses and thirty camels when there is a plot in Yemen involving treachery (dhū mughdira) – that is, when there is a plot involving treachery from them – and whatever of the horses or mounts they lent to my messengers perishes, they are responsible for until they return it to them. For Najrān and its environs is the protection of God and the covenant of Muḥammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, over their persons, their community, their land, their property, their absent and their present, their [other] folk, their missions and their amthila (2). What they were upon shall not be changed, nor shall any right of their rights or amthila be changed. No bishop shall be removed from his bishopric, no monk from his monasticism, nor any wāqih from his wāqihiyya, over whatever is in their hands, little or much. No oppression (rahaq) nor blood-vengeance of the Jāhiliyya shall be upon them; they shall not be mustered nor tithed; no army shall tread their land. Whoever among them asks for a right, there shall be equity between them, neither wronging nor wronged, in Najrān. Whoever of them consumes usury from before, my protection is clear of him. No man shall be seized for the wrong of another. For them, on what is in this document, is the protection of God and the covenant of Muḥammad the Prophet forever, until God's command comes, so long as they are sincere and make right what is incumbent upon them, not burdened with anything unjustly."

Witnessed: Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb, Ghaylān b. ʿAmr, and Mālik b. ʿAwf of the Banū Naṣr, al-Aqraʿ b. Ḥābis al-Ḥanẓalī, and al-Mughīra; and he wrote.

Yaḥyā b. Ādam said: I have seen a document in the hands of the Najrānīs whose text was similar to this text, and at its foot was "and ʿAlī b. Abū Ṭālib wrote it," and I do not know what to say about it.

(1) Q 3:58 ff. (2) In the margin of the manuscript: "amthila: the crosses and images."

201 – They said: When Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ became caliph, he held them to that. He wrote them a document along the lines of the Messenger of God's document ﷺ.

When ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ became caliph, they had taken up usury and multiplied. He feared them for Islam, so he expelled them and wrote for them: "To proceed: whoever of the people of Syria and Iraq they come upon, let him give them ample room from the land to till, and whatever they work shall be theirs in place of their land in Yemen." So they dispersed. Some settled in Syria, and some settled in al-Najrāniyya in the district of al-Kūfa, and it was named after them. The Jews of Najrān had entered with the Christians into the treaty, being like their dependants.

When ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān became caliph, he wrote to al-Walīd b. ʿUqba b. Abī Muʿayṭ, his governor over al-Kūfa: "To proceed: the ʿĀqib, the bishop (usquf) and the nobles of Najrān came to me with the Messenger of God's document ﷺ and showed me ʿUmar's condition. I asked ʿUthmān b. Ḥunayf about that, and he informed me he had investigated their affair and found it harmful to the dahāqīn (Persian landlords), restraining them from their land. I have remitted for them from their tribute two hundred ḥullas for the sake of God, and as a good outcome for them from their land. I commend them to you, for they are a people with a covenant of protection."

Cairo page 79

202 – I heard some of the scholars mention that ʿUmar wrote for them: "To proceed: whoever of the people of Syria and Iraq they come upon, let him give them ample room from the tillage of the land." And I heard some of them say: "from a jarīb of land."

203 – ʿAbd al-Aʿlā b. Ḥammād al-Narsī related to me: Ḥammād b. Salama told us, from Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd, from Ismāʿīl b. Ḥakīm, from ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said during his illness: Let not two religions remain in the land of the Arabs. When ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ became caliph, he expelled the people of Najrān to al-Najrāniyya and bought their landed properties and their wealth.

204 – al-ʿAbbās b. Hishām al-Kalbī related to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Najrān of Yemen was named after Najrān b. Zayd b. Saba' b. Yashjub b. Yaʿrub b. Qaḥṭān.

205 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: Wakīʿ b. al-Jarrāḥ told us: al-Aʿmash told us, from Sālim b. Abī l-Jaʿd, who said: The people of Najrān had reached forty thousand, and they envied one another, so they came to ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ and said: Expel us. ʿUmar had feared them for the Muslims, so he seized the opportunity and expelled them. They regretted it afterwards and came to him and said: Release us from it. He refused. When ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib ﵁ rose [to the caliphate], they came to him and said: We adjure you by your handwriting with your right hand and your intercession for us with your Prophet, to release us. He said: ʿUmar was right-minded in his decisions and I dislike opposing him.

Cairo page 80

206 – Abū Masʿūd al-Kūfī related to me: Muḥammad b. Marwān and al-Haytham b. ʿAdī told me, from al-Kalbī, that the head of al-Najrāniyya in al-Kūfa used to send his agents to all the Najrānīs in Syria and the districts, who collected money from them which he apportioned among them to maintain the ḥullas. When Muʿāwiya, or Yazīd b. Muʿāwiya, took office, they complained to him of their dispersal, the death of those who had died and the conversion of those who had converted, and they presented him with ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān's letter reducing their ḥullas, saying: We have only grown in decrease and weakness. He remitted two hundred ḥullas for them, completing four hundred ḥullas.

When al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf took charge of Iraq and Ibn al-Ashʿath rebelled against him, he suspected the dahāqīn of loyalty to him and suspected them with them, so he returned them to eighteen hundred ḥullas and required of them patterned (washy) ḥullas.

When ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz took office, they complained to him of their extinction and decline, the Bedouins' incessant raiding of them, their imposing on them burdens that crushed them, and al-Ḥajjāj's wronging them. He ordered a census, and they were found to be a tenth of their original number. He said: I consider this peace-settlement a poll-tax on their heads, not a peace for their lands, and the poll-tax of the dead and the convert lapses. So he imposed on them two hundred ḥullas, worth eight thousand dirhams.

When Yūsuf b. ʿUmar took over Iraq in the days of al-Walīd b. Yazīd he returned them to their former state, out of partisanship for al-Ḥajjāj.

When the Commander of the Faithful Abū l-ʿAbbās ﵀ became caliph, they made for his path on the day he appeared in al-Kūfa and threw basil on it and scattered it before him as he returned from the mosque to his residence. He was pleased with what they did. Then they presented to him their case, informing him of their paucity and what had been done by ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Yūsuf b. ʿUmar, and said: We have kinship with your maternal uncles, the Banū l-Ḥārith b. Kaʿb. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Rabīʿ al-Ḥārithī spoke for them, and al-Ḥajjāj b. Arṭāt confirmed what they claimed, so Abū l-ʿAbbās, God's blessings upon him, returned them to two hundred ḥullas valued at eight thousand dirhams.

Abū Masʿūd said: When al-Rashīd Hārūn became Commander of the Faithful and travelled to al-Kūfa on his way to the Hajj, they presented their case to him and complained of the governors' harshness toward them. He ordered a document written for them for the two hundred ḥullas, which I have seen, and ordered that they be exempted from dealing with the governors and that what they pay go to the treasury in the capital.

207 – ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb al-Miṣrī informed us, from Yūnus b. Yazīd, from Ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, who said: "And fight them until there is no more fitna and the religion is God's" (1) was revealed regarding the disbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs; and "Fight those who do not believe in God nor in the Last Day, nor forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, nor follow the religion of truth" – up to "and are humbled" (2) – was revealed regarding the People of the Book. The first of the People of the Book to give the poll-tax, as far as we know, were the people of Najrān, who were Christians; then the people of Ayla, Adhruḥ and Adhriʿāt gave the poll-tax in the Tabūk expedition.

(1) Q 2:193 (2) Q 9:29

Cairo page 82

Chapter 15

Yemen

208 – They said: When the news of the Messenger of God's emergence and the supremacy of his truth reached the people of Yemen, their delegations came to him . He wrote for them a document confirming them in what they had become Muslim upon, of their property, lands and buried treasure, and they became Muslim. He sent his messengers and governors to teach them the laws and sunan of Islam, to collect their ṣadaqas, and to levy the poll-tax on those of them who remained Christian, Jewish or Zoroastrian.

209 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Wakīʿ b. al-Jarrāḥ told us: Yazīd b. Ibrāhīm al-Tustarī told us, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to the people of Yemen: Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qibla and eats our slaughtered meat, that is the Muslim; he has the protection of God and the protection of His Messenger. Whoever refuses, upon him is the poll-tax.

210 – Hudba related to me: Yazīd b. Ibrāhīm told us, from al-Ḥasan, the like of it.

211 – Al-Wāqidī said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Khālid b. Saʿīd b. al-ʿĀṣ as governor to Ṣanʿāʾ and its land. He said: Some say the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed al-Muhājir b. Abī Umayya b. al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī over Ṣanʿāʾ, and was taken [in death] while he held it. He said: Others say that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ was the one who appointed al-Muhājir over Ṣanʿāʾ, and appointed Khālid b. Saʿīd over the districts of upper Yemen.

Cairo page 83

212 – Hishām b. al-Kalbī and al-Haytham b. ʿAdī said: The Messenger of God ﷺ appointed al-Muhājir over Kinda and al-Ṣadif. When the Messenger of God ﷺ was taken, Abū Bakr wrote to Ziyād b. Labīd al-Bayāḍī, of the Anṣār, appointing him over Kinda and al-Ṣadif in addition to what he governed of Ḥaḍramawt. He appointed al-Muhājir over Ṣanʿāʾ, then wrote to him to reinforce Ziyād b. Labīd, without removing him from Ṣanʿāʾ.

213 – They all agreed that the Messenger of God ﷺ appointed Ziyād b. Labīd over Ḥaḍramawt.

214 – They said: The Prophet ﷺ appointed Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī over Zabīd, Rimaʿ, ʿAdan and the coast. He appointed Muʿādh b. Jabal over al-Janad, assigned the judgeship to him, and made him collect all the ṣadaqas in Yemen. He appointed ʿAmr b. Ḥazm al-Anṣārī over Najrān; and it is said he appointed Abū Sufyān b. Ḥarb over Najrān after ʿAmr b. Ḥazm.

215 – ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṣāliḥ the Qurʾān-reciter informed me, saying: A trustworthy person related to me, from Ibn Lahīʿa, from Abū l-Aswad, from ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to Zurʿa b. Dhī Yazan:

"To proceed: when my messenger Muʿādh b. Jabal and his companions come to you, gather what you have of ṣadaqa and poll-tax and hand it over to him, for the leader of my messengers is Muʿādh, and he is among the righteous of those before me. Mālik b. Murāra al-Rahāwī has told me that you became Muslim, first of Ḥimyar, and separated from the polytheists; so receive good tidings. I command you, people of Ḥimyar, not to betray and not to oppose, for the Messenger of God is the patron of your rich and your poor. Ṣadaqa is not lawful for Muḥammad nor for his family; it is only zakāt by which you purify yourselves, for the poor of the Muslims and the believers. Mālik has brought the news and guarded the unseen; and Muʿādh is among the righteous of my family and those of their religion, so I commend him to you for good, for he is one to be looked up to. Peace."

216 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz told us, from ʿAmr b. ʿUthmān b. Mawhab, who said: I heard Mūsā b. Ṭalḥa say: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Muʿādh b. Jabal over the ṣadaqas of Yemen, and ordered him to take from dates, wheat, barley and grapes – or he said raisins – the tithe and the half-tithe.

217 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Ziyād told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, that the Messenger of God ﷺ wrote for ʿAmr b. Ḥazm when he sent him to Yemen: "In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. This is a declaration from God and His Messenger: 'O you who believe, fulfil the contracts' (1). A covenant from Muḥammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to ʿAmr b. Ḥazm when he sent him to Yemen: he commanded him to fear God in all his affairs, and to take from the spoils the fifth of God, and what is prescribed for the believers of ṣadaqa on landed produce: a tenth of what is watered by rain-fed (baʿl) and by rain, and a half-tithe of what is watered by the bucket (gharb)."

(1) Q 5:1.

Cairo page 85

218 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: Ziyād b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Bakkāʾī told us, from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to the kings of Ḥimyar: "In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful: From Muḥammad the Prophet, the Messenger of God, to al-Ḥārith b. ʿAbd Kulāl, Nuʿaym b. ʿAbd Kulāl, Sharḥ b. ʿAbd Kulāl, and to al-Nuʿmān, the qayl of Dhū Ruʿayn, Maʿāfir and Hamdān. To proceed: God has guided you with His guidance, if you act rightly and obey God and His Messenger, establish prayer, and pay zakāt: from the spoils the fifth of God and the share of the Prophet and his choice portion (ṣafī), and what God has prescribed for the believers of ṣadaqa on landed produce: a tenth of what the spring and the rain water, and a half-tithe of what is watered by the bucket."

219 – Hishām b. Muḥammad al-Kalbī said: The letter of the Messenger of God ﷺ was to ʿUrayb and al-Ḥārith, sons of ʿAbd Kulāl b. ʿUrayb b. Layshraḥ.

220 – Yūsuf b. Mūsā al-Qaṭṭān told us: Jarīr b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd told us: Manṣūr told us, from al-Ḥakam, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to Muʿādh b. Jabal while he was in Yemen: On what the rain waters, or what is watered by flowing water (ghayl), the tithe; on what is watered by the bucket and the water-wheel (dāliya), a half-tithe; on every adult a dinar or its equivalent in Maʿāfir cloth; and that no Jew be tempted away from his Judaism.

Cairo page 86

They said: Ghayl is sayḥ (flowing surface water); gharb is the bucket – meaning what is watered by sawānī, dawālī, dawālīb and gharrāfāt [all water-lifting devices]; baʿl is also sayḥ; and the maʿāfir are cloths of theirs.

221 – Abū ʿUbayd told us: Marwān b. Muʿāwiya told us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abū Wāʾil, from Masrūq, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Muʿādh to Yemen and ordered him to take from every thirty cattle a tabīʿ (yearling), from every forty a musinna (two-year-old), and from every adult a dinar or its equivalent in Maʿāfir cloth.

222 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Shaybān al-Burjumī told me, from ʿAmr, from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ took the poll-tax from the Magians of Hajar and the Magians of Yemen, and imposed on every one of the Yemeni Magians who reached puberty, man or woman, a dinar or its value in Maʿāfir cloth.

223 – ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb, from Maslama b. ʿAlī, from al-Muthannā b. al-Ṣabbāḥ, from ʿAmr b. Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of God ﷺ imposed the poll-tax on every adult (muḥtalim) of the people of Yemen: a dinar.

224 – Shaybān b. Abī Shayba al-Ubullī told us: Qazaʿa b. Suwayd al-Bāhilī told us: I heard Zakariyyā b. Isḥāq relate, from Yaḥyā b. Ṣayfī or Abū Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Muʿādh b. Jabal to Yemen he said: "You are going to a people of the People of the Book. Tell them: God has made obligatory upon you five prayers in the day and night. If they obey you, tell them: God has made obligatory upon you the fast of Ramaḍān in the year. If they obey you, tell them: God has made obligatory upon you the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find a way to it. If they obey you, tell them: God has made obligatory upon you in your property a ṣadaqa to be taken from your rich and returned to your poor. If they obey you, then beware of the choicest of their property. And beware the supplication of the wronged, for between it and God there is no veil nor screen."

Cairo page 87

225 – Shaybān told us: Ḥammād b. Salama told us: al-Ḥajjāj b. Arṭāt told us, from ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd Allāh, that al-Mughīra b. ʿAbd Allāh said: al-Ḥajjāj said: Assess every green thing. Abū Burda b. Abī Mūsā said: He is right. Mūsā b. Ṭalḥa said to Abū Burda: This one now claims that his father was among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ [?]. The Messenger of God ﷺ sent Muʿādh b. Jabal to Yemen and ordered him to take the ṣadaqa from dates, wheat, barley and raisins.

226 – ʿAmr al-Nāqid related to me: Wakīʿ told us, from ʿAmr b. ʿUthmān, from Mūsā b. Ṭalḥa b. ʿUbayd Allāh, who said: I read the letter of Muʿādh b. Jabal when the Messenger of God ﷺ sent him to Yemen, and in it was that ṣadaqa be taken from wheat, barley, dates, raisins and sorghum.

227 – ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Madīnī told us: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, who said: I asked Mujāhid why ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb ﵁ imposed more poll-tax on the people of Syria than he imposed on the people of Yemen. He said: Because of [their] wealth.

Cairo page 88

228 – al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad told us: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Ibrāhīm b. Maysara, from Ṭāwūs, who said: When Muʿādh came to Yemen, he was brought awqāṣ (odd lots below the taxable threshold) of cattle and honey, and he said: I was not ordered anything concerning this.

229 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mubārak told us, from Maʿmar, from Yaḥyā b. Qays al-Māzinī, from a man, from Abyaḍ b. Ḥammāl, that he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ to grant him the salt that is at Mārib as a fief. A man said: It is like flowing water [i.e., a perennial common resource]. So he refused to grant it to him.

230 – al-Qāsim b. Sallām and others related to me, from Ismāʿīl b. ʿAyyāsh, from ʿAmr b. Yaḥyā b. Qays al-Māzinī, from his father, from one who related to him, from Abyaḍ b. Ḥammāl, likewise.

231 – Aḥmad b. Ibrāhīm al-Dawraqī related to me: Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī told us: Shuʿba told us, from Simāk, from ʿAlqama b. Wāʾil al-Ḥaḍramī, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ granted him land in Ḥaḍramawt as a fief.

232 – ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Abī Sayf, freedman of Quraysh, related to me, from Maslama b. Muḥārib, who said: When Muḥammad b. Yūsuf, brother of al-Ḥajjāj b. Yūsuf, governed Yemen, he behaved badly, wronged the subjects and took people's lands unjustly. Among what he seized was al-Ḥarja. He said: And he imposed a kharāj on the people of Yemen, making it a fixed levy upon them. When ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz took office he wrote to his governor ordering him to abolish that levy and limit [collection] to the tithe, and said: By God, that no handful of katam (a dye plant) should come to me from Yemen is dearer to me than leaving this levy in place. When Yazīd b. ʿAbd al-Malik took office he ordered it restored.

Cairo page 89

233 – al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad al-Zaʿfarānī related to me, from al-Shāfiʿī, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān Hishām b. Yūsuf, judge of Ṣanʿāʾ, that the people of Khafāsh produced a letter from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq ﵁ on a piece of tanned leather, ordering them to pay the ṣadaqa on wars (a yellow dye plant).

Mālik, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, all the jurists of the Ḥijāz, Sufyān al-Thawrī and Abū Yūsuf said: There is no zakāt on wars, wasma (indigo), safflower (qurṭ), katam, henna and roses.

Abū Ḥanīfa said: On a small or large amount of those, zakāt is due.

Mālik said: On saffron, when its price reaches two hundred dirhams and it is sold, five dirhams. That is also Abū l-Zinād's view. It is also related from him that he said: Nothing is due on saffron.

Abū Ḥanīfa and Zufar said: On a small or large amount, zakāt is due.

Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan said: If its price reaches the lowest price of five awsuq of dates, wheat, barley, sorghum or any kind of grains, then ṣadaqa is due on it.

Ibn Abī Laylā said: Nothing is due on greens; this is also al-Shaʿbī's view.

ʿAṭāʾ and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: On whatever tithe-land produces, small or large, the tithe or half-tithe is due.

234 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Saʿīd b. Sālim, from al-Ṣalt b. Dīnār, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās in Basra used to take our ṣadaqas, even bundles of leeks.

Cairo page 90

235 – al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Ibn al-Mubārak told us, from Maʿmar, from Ṭāwūs and ʿIkrima, that they said: There is no zakāt on wars or on ʿuṭb – which is cotton.

Abū Ḥanīfa and Bishr said regarding dhimmīs who come to own tithe-lands, such as Yemen, whose people became Muslim upon it, and Basra, which the Muslims revived, and what the caliphs granted as fiefs in which no Muslim or covenant-protected person has any right: they are subject to the poll-tax on their persons, and kharāj is placed on their land according to its capacity, and what is collected from them goes the way of kharāj revenue; and if one of them becomes Muslim the poll-tax is lifted from him and kharāj remains on his land forever, on the analogy of the Sawād. This is also the view of Ibn Abī Laylā.

Ibn Shubruma and Abū Yūsuf said: The poll-tax is placed on their persons, and on their land they owe double what Muslims owe, which is a fifth or a tenth [i.e., double the tithe]. They based this on the case of the Christians of the Banū Taghlib.

Abū Yūsuf said: What is taken from them goes the way of kharāj; if the dhimmī becomes Muslim or his land passes to a Muslim, it becomes tithe-land. That is related from ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan.

Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, Ibn Abī Sabra, Sharīk b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Nakhaʿī and al-Shāfiʿī said: They owe the poll-tax on their persons, and neither kharāj nor tithe on their land, because they are not among those on whom zakāt is due, and their land is not kharāj land. That is also al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ b. Ḥayy al-Hamdānī's view.

Sufyān al-Thawrī and Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan said: They owe the tithe, not doubled, because the ruling follows the land and the owner is not considered.

Al-Awzāʿī and Sharīk b. ʿAbd Allāh said: If they are dhimmīs, like the Jews of Yemen, whose people became Muslim while they were there, you take nothing from them but the poll-tax, and you do not allow the dhimmī to buy land from the tithe-lands or enter into it – meaning to own it by that.

Cairo page 91

Al-Wāqidī said: I asked Mālik about a Jew of the Jews of the Ḥijāz who buys land at al-Jurf and sows it. He said: The tithe is taken from him. I said: Do you not claim there is no tithe on a dhimmī's land if he owns tithe-land? He said: That is when they remain in their own country; but when they leave their country, it is trade.

Abū l-Zinād, Mālik b. Anas, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb, al-Thawrī, Abū Ḥanīfa and Yaʿqūb said, of a Taghlibī who farms tithe-land: double the tithe is taken from him. If a man rents a tithe-farm, Mālik, al-Thawrī, Ibn Abī Dhiʾb and Yaʿqūb said: The tithe is on the owner of the crop. Abū Ḥanīfa said: It is on the owner of the land; and that is Zufar's view.

Abū Ḥanīfa said: If a man does not pay the tithe of his land for two years, the authority takes the tithe from him for what [crop] he starts afresh, and likewise kharāj land. Abū Shumr (?) said: He takes that from him for what has passed, because it is a right that became due on his property .

Cairo page 92

Chapter 16

ʿUmān

ʿUmān (Oman)

236 – They said: The Azd predominated in ʿUmān, though many people of other [tribes] were there too, in the desert regions. In the year 8 the Messenger of God ﷺ sent Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī, of the Khazraj, who was one of those who had collected the Qurʾān in the lifetime of the Messenger of God ﷺ – his name, according to al-Kalbī, was Qays b. Sakan b. Zayd b. Ḥarām; some Basrans say his name was ʿAmr b. Akhṭab, grandfather of ʿUrwa b. Thābit b. ʿAmr b. Akhṭab; and Saʿīd b. Aws al-Anṣārī said his name was Thābit b. Zayd – and he sent ʿAmr b. al-ʿĀṣ al-Sahmī to ʿAbd and Jayfar, sons of al-Julandā, with a letter from him calling them to Islam, saying: If the people respond to the testimony of truth and obey God and His Messenger, then ʿAmr is the commander, and Abū Zayd is in charge of prayer, of administering Islam to the people and teaching them the Qurʾān and the sunan. When Abū Zayd and ʿAmr reached ʿUmān they found ʿAbd and Jayfar at Ṣuḥār on the seacoast. They delivered the Prophet's letter ﷺ to them; they became Muslim and called the Arabs there to Islam, who responded and were eager for it. ʿAmr and Abū Zayd remained in ʿUmān until the Prophet ﷺ was taken. It is said that Abū Zayd came to Medina before that.

237 – They said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ was taken, the Azd apostatized under Laqīṭ b. Mālik Dhū l-Tāj and withdrew to Dabā – some say Dimā in Dabā. Abū Bakr ﵁ sent against them Ḥudhayfa b. Miḥṣan al-Bāriqī of the Azd and ʿIkrima b. Abī Jahl b. Hishām al-Makhzūmī; they engaged Laqīṭ and those with him, killed him, and took captives of the people of Dabā, whom they sent to Abū Bakr ﵀. Then the Azd returned to Islam,

Cairo page 93

while groups of the people of ʿUmān apostatized and joined al-Shiḥr. ʿIkrima marched against them, defeated them, took booty from them and killed many. A group of Mahra b. Ḥaydān b. ʿAmr b. al-Ḥāf b. Quḍāʿa had assembled a force; ʿIkrima came to them and they did not fight him and paid the ṣadaqa. Abū Bakr ﵁ appointed Ḥudhayfa b. Miḥṣan over ʿUmān; Abū Bakr died while he held it; [Ḥudhayfa] dismissed ʿIkrima, who was sent to Yemen. ʿUmān remained in good order, its people paying the ṣadaqas of their property and the poll-tax being taken from the protected people there, until the caliphate of al-Rashīd, may God's blessings be on him, who appointed over it ʿĪsā b. Jaʿfar b. Sulaymān b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAbbās. He went to it with the people of Basra, who began to commit fornication with the women, plunder them and display musical instruments. This reached the people of ʿUmān, most of whom were shurāt (Khārijites), so they fought him and barred him from entering it, then overpowered him, killed and crucified him, and withheld obedience from the authorities, appointing one of themselves over their affairs.

Some say that the Messenger of God ﷺ had sent Abū Zayd with his letter to ʿAbd and Jayfar, sons of al-Julandā, the two Azdīs, in the year 6, and sent ʿAmr in the year 8, shortly after his conversion. His conversion, and that of Khālid b. al-Walīd and ʿUthmān b. Ṭalḥa al-ʿAbdarī, was in Ṣafar of the year 8; he came from Abyssinia and went to the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of God ﷺ said to Abū Zayd: Take the ṣadaqa from the Muslims and the poll-tax from the Magians.

238 – Abū l-Ḥasan al-Madāʾinī related to me, from al-Mubārak b. Fuḍāla, who said: ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to ʿAdī b. Arṭāt al-Fazārī, his governor over Basra:

Cairo page 94

"To proceed: I had written to ʿAmr b. ʿAbd Allāh to divide what was found in ʿUmān of the tithes of dates and grain among its poor, and those who had dropped into it from the Bedouin, and those whom need, destitution and being cut off on the road had brought to it. He wrote back to me that he had asked your governor before him about that food and those dates, and he mentioned that he had sold it and carried its price to you. So return to ʿAmr what your governor over ʿUmān carried to you of the price of the dates and grain, so that he may place it in the places I commanded him and spend it in them, God willing. Peace."

Cairo page 95

Chapter 17

Al-Baḥrayn

al-Baḥrayn (Bahrain)

239 – They said: The land of al-Baḥrayn belonged to the Persian kingdom, and many Arabs of ʿAbd al-Qays, Bakr b. Wāʾil and Tamīm lived in its desert regions. Over the Arabs there, on behalf of the Persians, in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ was al-Mundhir b. Sāwā, of the Banū ʿAbd Allāh b. Zayd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Dārim b. Mālik b. Ḥanẓala – this ʿAbd Allāh b. Zayd being al-Asbadhī, named after a village in Hajar called al-Asbadh; it is also said he was named after the Asbadhīs, a people who worshipped horses in al-Baḥrayn. In the year 8 the Messenger of God ﷺ sent al-ʿAlāʾ b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿImād al-Ḥaḍramī, ally of the Banū ʿAbd Shams, to al-Baḥrayn to call its people to Islam or the poll-tax, and wrote with him to al-Mundhir b. Sāwā and to Sībukht, the marzbān of Hajar, calling them to Islam or the poll-tax. They became Muslim, and with them all the Arabs there and some of the non-Arabs. As for the people of the land, Magians, Jews and Christians, they made peace with al-ʿAlāʾ, who wrote between himself and them a document, whose text is:

"In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. This is what al-ʿAlāʾ b. al-Ḥaḍramī settled with the people of al-Baḥrayn: he settled with them that they spare us the labour and share the dates with us; whoever does not fulfil this, upon him is the curse of God, the angels and all people."

As for the poll-tax on persons, he took for it a dinar from every adult .

240 – ʿAbbās b. Hishām related to me, from his father, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to the people of al-Baḥrayn:

Cairo page 96

"To proceed: if you establish prayer, pay zakāt, give sincere counsel to God and His Messenger, pay the tithe of the palms and the half-tithe of grain, and do not Magianize your children, then you keep what you became Muslim upon, except that the fire-temple belongs to God and His Messenger; and if you refuse, upon you is the poll-tax."

The Magians and Jews disliked Islam and preferred paying the poll-tax. The hypocrites of the Arabs said: Muḥammad claims he accepts the poll-tax only from the People of the Book, yet he has accepted it from the Magians of Hajar, who are not People of the Book. So there was revealed: "O you who believe, you are responsible for yourselves; those who go astray cannot harm you if you are guided" (1).

It is also said that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent al-ʿAlāʾ when he sent his envoys to the kings in the year 6.

241 – Muḥammad b. Muṣaffā al-Ḥimṣī related to me: Muḥammad b. al-Mubārak told us: ʿAttāb b. Ziyād told us: Muḥammad b. Maymūn told me, from Mughīra al-Azdī, from Muḥammad b. Zayd b. Ḥayyān al-Aʿraj, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. al-Ḥaḍramī, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent me to al-Baḥrayn – or he said Hajar – and I would come to the walled garden shared among brothers, some of whom had become Muslim, and I would take the tithe from the Muslim and the kharāj from the polytheist.

242 – al-Qāsim b. Sallām told us: ʿUthmān b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Lahīʿa, from Abū l-Aswad, from ʿUrwa b. al-Zubayr, that the Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to the people of Hajar: In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. From Muḥammad the Prophet to the people of Hajar. Peace be upon you. I praise to you God, besides whom there is no god. To proceed: I commend you to God and to yourselves, that you not go astray after being guided, nor err after being rightly directed.

(1) Q 5:105

Cairo page 97

To proceed: what you have done has reached me; whoever of you does good, the sin of the wrongdoer is not laid on him. When my governors come to you, obey them and support them and help them in God's command and in His cause; whoever of you does righteous work will not lose it with God and with me. To proceed: your delegation came to me and I did nothing to them but what pleased them; and had I exerted my full right over you, I would have expelled you from Hajar; but I interceded for your absent and favoured your present. "So remember the favour of God upon you" (1).

243 – al-Ḥusayn b. al-Aswad related to me: ʿUbayd Allāh b. Mūsā told us, from Shaybān al-Naḥwī, from Qatāda, who said: There was no fighting in al-Baḥrayn in the days of the Messenger of God ﷺ; rather, some of them became Muslim and some made peace with al-ʿAlāʾ on halves of the grain and dates.

244 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told me: al-Ḥasan b. Ṣāliḥ told us, from Ashʿath, from al-Zuhrī, that the Messenger of God ﷺ took the poll-tax from the Magians of Hajar.

245 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us: Qays b. al-Rabīʿ told us, from Qays b. Muslim, from al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ wrote to the Magians of Hajar calling them to Islam: if they become Muslim, they have what we have and owe what we owe; and whoever refuses, upon him is the poll-tax, without eating their slaughtered meat or marrying their women.

246 – al-Ḥusayn related to me: Yaḥyā b. Ādam told us, from Ibn al-Mubārak, from Yūnus b. Yazīd al-Aylī, from al-Zuhrī, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyab, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ took the poll-tax from the Magians of Hajar; ʿUmar took it from the Magians of Persia; and ʿUthmān took it from the Berbers.

(1) A quotation from Q 2:231.

Cairo page 98

247 – al-Ḥusayn told us: Yaḥyā told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Idrīs told us, from Mālik b. Anas, from al-Zuhrī, likewise.

248 – ʿAmr al-Nāqid told us: ʿAbd Allāh b. Wahb informed us, from Yaḥyā b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Sālim b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUmar, from Mūsā b. ʿUqba, that the Prophet ﷺ wrote to Mundhir b.
